f64_castlevein.title: Castlevania
sents: lead
Castlevania (/ ˌ k æ s əl ˈ v eɪ n i ə /), known in Japan as Akumajō Dracula, is a gothic horror action-adventure video game series and media franchise created by Konami.
lead
The series is largely set in the eponymous castle of Count Dracula, the main antagonist of the Belmont clan of vampire hunters.
lead
Debuting with the 1986 video game on Nintendo 's Famicom Disk System, the first entry and the majority of its sequels are side-scrolling action platformers.
lead

The 1997 game, Castlevania: Symphony of the Night, originally released for the PlayStation, returned to the nonlinear gameplay first seen in Castlevania II: Simon's Quest; which also introduced role-playing elements and exploration.
lead
Several installments later adopted Symphony of the Night ' s gameplay, and along with Super Metroid, have popularized the Metroidvania genre.
lead
2010 saw the release of Castlevania: Lords of Shadow, a 3D action-adventure game developed by MercurySteam and Kojima Productions that served as a reboot of the series.
lead
The Castlevania series has been released on various platforms; from early systems to modern consoles, as well as handheld devices such as mobile phones.
lead
The franchise has since expanded into several spin-off video games and other media; including comic books and a critically-acclaimed animated television series.
Games

Most Castlevania titles have been released in Japan, North America, Europe and Australia on various video game consoles, personal computers (PC) and mobile phones, with additional remakes and re-releases.
Games
The first console title, Castlevania, was released on the Famicom Disk System in 1986 and in North America in 1987 on the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES).
Games
A 2D sidescrolling action game where the player progresses through six stages, many principal features of the Castlevania series originated with it.
Games

Following that year, in 1987, Castlevania II: Simon's Quest further departed from the standard platforming genre of the first Castlevania for a game more similar to the nonlinear gameplay of Metroid, with several role-playing elements such as a world map which the player is free to explore and revisit.
Games
Haunted Castle (1988), the franchise's first arcade title, returned to the linear platforming gameplay of the original.
Games
This continued with the first handheld Game Boy entry, Castlevania: The Adventure and the NES sequel, Castlevania III: Dracula's Curse, both released in 1989.
Games
The Adventure saw a Game Boy sequel, Castlevania II: Belmont's Revenge, in 1992 and a remake, Castlevania: The Adventure ReBirth, developed by M2 for the WiiWare service in 2009.
Games
The franchise's first 16-bit home console game, Super Castlevania IV, was released for the Super Nintendo Entertainment System (SNES) in 1991.
Games
A Castlevania title for the Sharp X68000 home computer was released in Japan in 1993 and would not be available in English until Castlevania Chronicles (2001) for the PlayStation.
Games

During the same year, Castlevania: Rondo of Blood was released for the PC Engine and was not localized in English until it was included with Castlevania: The Dracula X Chronicles (2007) for the PlayStation Portable.
Games
The first Castlevania produced for a CD-ROM, Rondo of Blood featured Red Book audio and fully voiced dialogue.
Games
The game's content would be reused in Castlevania: Dracula X, a game for the SNES in 1995.
Games
Castlevania: Bloodlines (1994) was the first Castlevania entry produced for a Sega console, the Genesis.
Games
In 1997, Castlevania: Symphony of the Night and Castlevania Legends were launched for the PlayStation and Game Boy, respectively.
Games

Elements of Symphony of the Night would influence the gameplay of future titles, beginning with the Game Boy Advance entries Circle of the Moon, Harmony of Dissonance, and Aria of Sorrow, which were released from 2001 to 2003.
Games
Aria of Sorrow received a 2005 sequel, Dawn of Sorrow for the Nintendo DS, which was followed by Portrait of Ruin (2006) and Order of Ecclesia (2008).
Games

Under the development of Konami's Kobe branch, the first game in the series to employ 3D graphics was Castlevania for Nintendo 64 in 1999, and it received an expansion called Castlevania: Legacy of Darkness later that year.
Games

In 2003, the next 3D Castlevania title, Lament of Innocence debuted for the PlayStation 2 with combat-oriented hack and slash gameplay that drew comparisons to Devil May Cry and retroactively, God of War.
Games
A reboot of the franchise launched with Castlevania: Lords of Shadow in 2010, a multi-platform 3D action title developed by MercurySteam and co-produced by Hideo Kojima.
Games
It was followed by two sequels, Lords of Shadow – Mirror of Fate for Nintendo 3DS in 2013, and Lords of Shadow 2 in 2014.
Games
Lords of Shadow 2 was the last mainline game in the franchise to date, due to Konami shifting focus to mobile games and gambling in the 2010s.
Games
Rumors began circulating in 2021 that, following internal restructuring at Konami to refocus on PC and console games, a "reimagining" of the series was in development.
Games
In 2024, a remake of Haunted Castle was included in the compilation Castlevania Dominus Collection.
Games
Titled Haunted Castle Revisited, it was developed by M2, who previously worked on The Adventure ReBirth.
Spin-offs
Castlevania has spawned numerous spin-offs, the first being the 1990 platformer, Kid Dracula for the Famicom, a parody which stars the eponymous character.
Spin-offs
It was released for the first time in English for the Castlevania Anniversary Collection (2019).
Spin-offs
Castlevania ' s first fighting game, Castlevania Judgment debuted for the Wii in 2008 and was developed by Eighting.
Spin-offs
Castlevania: Harmony of Despair, released in 2010, was an online, multiplayer title in-which players could play as past Castlevania characters and explore stages.
Spin-offs
A mobile game called Castlevania: Grimoire of Souls was released on September 19, 2019 for iOS through Apple Arcade.
Spin-offs
Castlevania: The Arcade (2009), a light gun shooter utilizing an LED remote, has been released in Japan and Europe.
Spin-offs
The Japanese-exclusive Pachislot Akumajō Dracula series is a line of pachislot titles released between 2009 and 2017.
Spin-offs
The first three are based on the video game Dracula's Curse, while a fourth game based on the Lords of Shadow reboot, Pachislot Akumajō Dracula: Lords of Shadow, was made available in 2017.
Gameplay
Castlevania, released for the NES in 1986, is a platform game in which the player takes the role of the character Simon Belmont, navigating through six levels of Dracula's castle.
Gameplay
Loss of all health, falling off-screen, or running out of time results in losing a life, with the game ending when all lives are depleted, though players can continue from the last checkpoint.
Gameplay
Simon wields the Vampire Killer whip, which can be improved by collecting upgrades hidden in candles.
Gameplay

While Castlevania' s gameplay set the standard for most titles, Castlevania II: Simon's Quest in 1987 briefly introduced role-playing elements, a departure from the strict platforming format of its predecessor.
Gameplay
1997's Castlevania: Symphony of the Night significantly expanded upon the gameplay introduced in Simon's Quest, setting a new formula for the series and influencing subsequent Metroidvania titles.
Gameplay
The first 3D installment in the franchise, Castlevania (1999) on the Nintendo 64 adopted gameplay elements distinctly different from its 2D predecessors.
Gameplay

The new environment itself played a crucial role in the gameplay, with challenges based on precision in jumping across 3D platforms and navigating through hazardous areas, some of which included rotating and crumbling platforms.
Gameplay
Castlevania for the Nintendo 64 also incorporated elements of survival horror, such as a sequence where the player must run from a pursuing enemy in a hedge maze.
Gameplay
Unlike the earlier 3D installment which involved navigating through various levels with a degree of platforming challenge, 2003's Lament of Innocence focused on a central hub system.
Gameplay
The 2010 reboot, Lords of Shadow introduced a more diverse range of up to forty unlockable combos with the game's whip, the Combat Cross, integrating both direct and area attacks.
Plot and setting
Alucard, introduced in Castlevania III: Dracula's Curse, is a reference to the character of the same name from the 1943 film, Son of Dracula.
Plot and setting

Castlevania: Bloodlines explicitly incorporates the events of Bram Stoker 's Dracula into the series, and the recurring character Carmilla is based on the 1872 novel Carmilla by Joseph Sheridan Le Fanu.
Plot and setting
The Vampire Killer is a legendary whip that is passed down to their successors and can only be used by them.
Plot and setting
Castlevania: Lords of Shadow is a reboot of the franchise, with its first game set in Southern Europe during the Middle Ages.
Plot and setting
The sequel, Castlevania: Lords of Shadow 2 is set during modern times, where Dracula is looking for a way to put an end to his immortality.
Plot and setting

In 2002, the games Legends, Circle of the Moon, Castlevania (1999), and Legacy of Darkness were retconned from the official chronology by Koji Igarashi, a move which had been met with some criticism by fans.
Plot and setting
The American 20th Anniversary Pre-order Bundle for Portrait of Ruin in 2006 featured a poster with a timeline that re-included the games other than Legends.
Plot and setting
In 2007, Konami still excluded them from the canon on the official Japanese website.
Development
Castlevania was directed and programmed by Hitoshi Akamatsu for the Family Computer Disk System in 1986.
Development
After the success of Castlevania, it was released in cartridge format for the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES) as one of its first major platform games.
Development
Because of Nintendo of America's censorship policies at the time, most instances of blood, nudity and religious imagery were removed or edited in early Castlevania games.
Development
Akamatsu directed Castlevania II: Simon's Quest in 1987, which adopted gameplay similar to Nintendo's Metroid.
Development
His last game in the series, Castlevania III: Dracula's Curse (1989), returned to the standard platforming genre of Castlevania.
Development
In 1993, three Castlevania games were in parallel development, which included Akumajō Dracula, Rondo of Blood, and Bloodlines.
Development
Directed and produced by Toru Hagihara, Rondo of the Blood was the first installment made for a CD-ROM and the first to be fully voiced.
Development
Hagihara would go on to direct a sequel, Symphony of the Night (1997) for the PlayStation, with Koji Igarashi joining him as the assistant director and story writer.
Development
The gameplay took a departure from the original platforming entries, instead adopting nonlinear exploration and role-playing game elements, which were last seen in Simon's Quest.
Development
The first Castlevania game to feature 3D computer graphics began development in 1997 on the Nintendo 64 by Konami Computer Entertainment Kobe (KCEK) as Dracula 3D.
Development
Like most of its predecessors, it was an action-adventure and platforming game.
Development
KCEK's last Castlevania game was the acclaimed Circle of the Moon, released as a launch title for the Game Boy Advance in 2001.
Development
Circle of the Moon was the first entry to feature Metroidvania gameplay since Symphony of the Night.
Development
In 2002, he retconned Castlevania Legends (1997) and the games developed by KCEK from the series' chronology due to story conflicts, which was met with some resistance from fans.
Development

After KCEK was dissolved during 2002, the Game Boy Advance received a second installment, Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance, now produced by Igarashi and developed by Konami Computer Entertainment Tokyo (KCET).
Development
Konami eventually returned to the title Akumajō Dracula with the Japanese release of 2005's Castlevania: Dawn of Sorrow for the Nintendo DS.
Development
Konami told MercurySteam the game would be an original intellectual property (IP) when it was first greenlit as a Castlevania title.
Development
The art style departed from the previous games in favor of one inspired by Guillermo del Toro 's work.
Development
It was followed by two sequels, Mirror of Fate (2013) and Castlevania: Lords of Shadow 2 (2014).
Audio
The music for the first installment, Castlevania, was composed by Kinuyo Yamashita and Satoe Terashima.
Audio
Under strict hardware constraints, she would first write the scores before entering it as data into a computer.
Audio
The hardware for the first 16-bit title, Super Castlevania IV, allowed for a more atmospheric environment in the game, and was composed by Masanori Adachi and Taro Kudo.
Audio
Known primarily for her work on the Castlevania series, Michiru Yamane first composed music for the Sega Genesis game, Castlevania Bloodlines.
Audio
Before becoming a freelance composer, the last Castlevania game she scored was Castlevania: Order of Ecclesia in 2008, which she worked on with Yasuhiro Ichihashi.
Audio
For the 2010 reboot, Castlevania: Lords of Shadow, the game was scored by Óscar Araujo using a 120-piece orchestra.
Reception and legacy
The Castlevania franchise had sold over 20 million copies worldwide as of 2006; it had previously sold over 3.7 million units by 1993.
Reception and legacy

The franchise has received mostly positive reviews, with the most acclaimed game being Symphony of the Night for the PlayStation and the most panned being Judgment, with aggregate scores of 93 and 49, respectively, on Metacritic and 93.38% and 52.71%, respectively, on GameRankings.
Reception and legacy
Symphony of the Night appeared at #16 on IGN "Top 100 games" and was one of the first to be introduced on the GameSpot "The Greatest Games of All Time".
Reception and legacy
Castlevania III: Dracula's Curse was named the 9th best 8-bit game by GameTrailers.
Reception and legacy
Super Castlevania IV was named the 11th best game of the SNES by ScrewAttack on their " Top 20 SNES Games ".
Reception and legacy

The series as a whole was named the 4th best franchise in games ever by IGN, behind only Final Fantasy, The Legend of Zelda and Mario, and citing Super Castlevania IV and Symphony of the Night as highlights.
Reception and legacy
Trivia about the series has been mentioned in the Guinness World Records: Gamer's Edition 2008.
In other media
Dracula, referred to only as "the Count", appeared as a villain in Captain N.
In other media
Illustrated by Kou Sasakura, a two-volume manga adaptation titled Castlevania: Curse of Darkness, based on the PlayStation 2 installment, was published in Japan from 2005 to 2006.
In other media
2003's Lament of Innocence was adapted into a cellphone comic book, released exclusively in Japan from 2007-2008 for 40 episodes.
TV series
The streaming service Netflix released an American animated series titled Castlevania as part of its original programming between 2017 and 2021, consisting of four seasons and 32 episodes.
TV series
The series was created by Warren Ellis; in developing the series, Ellis relied heavily on a script he had written for an animated Castlevania film from 2007 that never entered production.
TV series
A sequel to the original show, Castlevania: Nocturne, was released on Netflix on September 28, 2023.
Cancelled projects
Only the Mario and The Legend of Zelda segments for the block were ultimately produced, airing in 1989 as part of The Super Mario Bros.
Cancelled projects
On May 27, 2009, the Castlevania film was reported as officially canceled.

Carrie and Reinhardt's quests are a secondary focus (bonus features), that can only be unlocked after completing both Cornell and Henry's quests.

Igarashi later clarified that he looks at the titles as "...a Castlevania "gaiden" (subseries)" and complimented them by stating "...they both have a really unique take on the Castlevania world."

Resident Evil 2 is a 1998 survival horror video game developed and published by Capcom for the PlayStation.
lead
The player controls rookie cop Leon S.
lead

Kennedy and college student Claire Redfield, who must escape Raccoon City after its citizens are transformed into zombies by a biological weapon two months after the events of the original Resident Evil.
lead

The gameplay focuses on exploration, puzzles, and combat; the main difference from its predecessor are the branching paths, with each player character having unique storylines, partners and obstacles.
lead
Resident Evil 2 was produced by Resident Evil director Shinji Mikami, directed by Hideki Kamiya, and developed by a team of approximately 50 across 21 months.
lead
The initial version, commonly referred to as Resident Evil 1.5, differs drastically; it was canceled at approximately two thirds completion because Mikami decided it was inadequate.
lead
The final design introduced a more cinematic presentation.
lead

Resident Evil 2 received acclaim for its atmosphere, setting, graphics, audio, scenarios, overall gameplay, and its improvements over the original game, but with some criticism towards its controls, voice acting, and certain gameplay elements.

Resident Evil 2 is a third-person survival horror game which features the same basic gameplay as its predecessor, Resident Evil.

While the player characters may be equipped with firearms, limited ammunition adds a tactical element to combat, forcing the player to choose between engaging or evading encounters.

Safe rooms scattered throughout the city contain typewriters, where the player may spend ink ribbons to save their progress, and item boxes that can store items, which are necessary because the player characters can only carry a limited number of items with them.
Gameplay
Contrasting with Chris and Jill's different abilities in the previous game, Leon and Claire differ only in their starting key items (a lighter and a lockpick, respectively).

In both, the player must reach the goal while fighting every enemy along the way with only the default item loadout.

On September 29, 1998, two months after the events of the first Resident Evil, most citizens of the Midwestern American mountain community of Raccoon City have been transformed into zombies by the T-virus, a biological weapon secretly developed by the pharmaceutical company Umbrella.
Plot
Kennedy, a Raccoon Police Department officer on his first day of duty, meets Claire Redfield, a college student looking for her brother Chris.
Plot
Leon, Ada, Claire, and Sherry advance through an abandoned factory connected to Umbrella's secret underground research facility.
Plot
Grown to gigantic size, William follows Leon and Claire, but is destroyed when the train self-destructs.
Development
Development of Resident Evil 2 began one month after the completion of its predecessor in early 1996.
Development
Resident Evil 2 was developed by a group of about 45 people that later became part of Capcom Production Studio 4.
Development
The game took more than $1 million to create.

Mikami also revealed in 1996 that the sequel would have new monsters, and the number of onscreen enemies would be increased to "around seven or more" to produce "the sensation of terror as the monsters swarm around the character".

Believing the game's assets were good individually, but not yet satisfactory as a whole, Mikami expected that everything would coalesce in the three months leading up to the projected May 1997 release date.
