Other gates are hidden throughout Great Tree, such as one in the library that is only accessible after befriending over 100 different monsters.
Breeding
After beating Class F in the Arena, the player can breed monsters if they are at level 10 or above at the Shrine of Starry Night, which is taken care of by the current Master Monster Tamer.
Breeding
The result of the breeding will be an egg, containing a level 1 monster which has characteristics of both parents, including skills and stats.
Breeding
Breeding is also the only way to acquire certain monsters.
Story
After his arrival, Terry met the King and received Slib the slime, his first monster to train.
Nintendo 3DS remake

The Nintendo 3DS remake was announced in September 2011 by publisher Square Enix, and was said to include new monsters, a new story, and additional monsters from Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker 2 Professional.
Nintendo 3DS remake
The game was shown as a playable demo at Jump Magazines Jump Festa in December 2011.
Nintendo 3DS remake

The game features include shifting from day to night, randomized dungeon layouts, combat with four opponents on each side, and a total of 609 monsters, including all the monsters from the original Game Boy Color release.
Nintendo 3DS remake
The store's items changes daily, and the Wi-Fi item store is only open after doing that day's Wi-Fi Ranking Battle.
Nintendo 3DS remake

Players have the ability to import monsters they have raised from Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker 2 and Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker 2 Professional (Rank A and higher only) through a free app upon completion of the game.
Nintendo 3DS remake
X and XY monsters (+, and +* in the original Japanese version) in Joker 2/Professional could be obtained by synthesizing 2 of the same monsters, level 20 for X, and level 50 for XY monsters.
Nintendo 3DS remake
Both duplicate monsters of different gender have to have their monster's rank points +25 for + monsters, and +50 for +* monsters.
Nintendo 3DS remake
In Dragon Quest Monsters: Terry's Wonderland 3D, there is a +, and +* for every monster, while in Joker 2/Professional not every monster had them.
Nintendo 3DS remake
Using the StreetPass feature of the Nintendo 3DS, players can fight other players and attempt to steal their monsters.
Nintendo 3DS remake
In B3 of the Great Tree, one of the two gates there goes to an arena where players can battle the top 3 users who've won that day's ranking battle.
Nintendo 3DS remake
If a player loses between 51-100, they get to start back at battle 50.
Reception
In Japan, Dragon Warrior Monsters sold 2.35 million copies, of which 1.22 million were sold during 1998—making it the fourth-highest selling game of the year.
Reception
The North American version sold 60,000 copies by April 2000.
Reception
Dragon Warrior Monsters received mostly positive reviews, receiving an average score of 78.9% from GameRankings based on 12 reviews.
Reception
PlayStation compilation Dragon Quest Monsters 1+2 received a 33 out of 40 by Famitsu magazine.
Reception
The game was the 38th best-selling game of 2002 with 292,275 copies.
Reception
The Nintendo 3DS remake sold 513,000 copies in its first week.
Reception
Publisher Square Enix sold through 93.96 percent of their stock and several stores sold out of product.
Reception
A special version of the Nintendo 3DS bundled with the game also sold 100,000 units in the first week.
Reception
As of January 2013, the game has 920,000 copies.
Reception

As a promotion, fast food franchise McDonald's gave away a Slanin Purple on May 31, 2012 in Happy Meals to those who had copies of the game, and on June 9 they gave away Ramia, a monster from Dragon Warrior III.

pboy_harvest_moo_gb.title: Harvest Moon GB
sents: lead
Harvest Moon GB (牧場物語GB, Bokujō Monogatari GB) is the second game in the Story of Seasons series of video games, and was developed and published by Victor Interactive Software.
lead
Harvest Moon GB is the first portable Harvest Moon game, developed for the Game Boy.
lead
A Game Boy Color version was released later under the name Harvest Moon GBC.
lead
The Game Boy Color version was later released on the 3DS Virtual Console in 2013.
Tools and items
At the beginning of the game, the tools available are the axe, hoe, hammer, watering can (obtained after buying the first crop seeds), and sickle.
Reception
Harvest Moon GB was fairly well received, earning a 7.2/10 review from Nintendo Power.

pboy_harvest_moo_2_gbc.title: Harvest Moon 2 GBC
sents: lead

Harvest Moon 2 GBC, released in Japan as Bokujō Monogatari GB2 (牧場物語GB2), is a farm simulation video game for the Game Boy Color developed and published by Victor Interactive Software, and the second portable game in the Story of Seasons series.
lead
The object of the game is to cultivate a farm to prevent the land from being used to build an amusement park.
lead
As with the previous game, the player may choose to play as a boy or a girl.
Gameplay
Some major differences between Harvest Moon GB and Harvest Moon 2 GBC is that in Harvest Moon 2 GBC one is able to build a sheep pen and buy sheep, build a greenhouse, and walk around the town.
Gameplay
At the end of the first year, the mayor of the city comes back to the farm to check up on it.
Animals

The player after a certain period of time (Fall 1st, First year, usually) is able to acquire a horse, which can be ridden (once it is an adult horse, which takes until the Second year, Spring 2nd) and used for farm work as well.
Animals
A cow with 8 or more hearts will produce Large Milk and a cow that has less than that will produce Small Milk.
Animals
Similar to cows, feeding them for 3 days straight should make them lay eggs again.
Animals
When sheep have a higher happiness rating, they produce large pieces of wool, which sell for 250G apiece.
Animals
As with cows, they become agitated (and stay grumpy) for three days if the farmer is unable to feed them; feeding them and shampooing them for 3 days straight should make them happy again.
Collecting and Trading
The game was the first in the series to introduce a wildlife collecting mechanic.
Collecting and Trading
For the first time fish were not categorized by size (small, medium, large) like in previous entries, but were instead categorized by their individual species.
Collecting and Trading
The player was also able to capture insects in the mountain area (a series first).
Collecting and Trading

The fish and insects that the player caught (as well as flowers that the player grew) could also be traded by Game Link Cable to other copies of Harvest Moon 2 GBC or to the game Legend of the River King 2.
Collecting and Trading
There were species of Fish, Insects, and Flowers that could only be obtained through trading.
Reception
IGN said that the game world is much bigger than the first Harvest Moon, and the farming much improved, but the dating sim aspect of the game is greatly missed.
Reception
In Japan, Famitsu gave it a score of 30 out of 40.

pboy_shanty.title: Shantae (video game)

Platform(s): Game Boy Color Nintendo Switch PlayStation 4 PlayStation 5

sents: lead
Shantae is a platform video game developed by WayForward and published by Capcom for the Game Boy Color in 2002.
lead
It is the first title in the Shantae series.
lead
The game follows the adventures of the eponymous half-genie Shantae, who must travel across Sequin Land, the setting of the series, to foil the domination plans of the evil lady pirate Risky Boots.
lead

During her quest, she learns various dances and acquires items which make her progressively stronger as well as unlocking new abilities and locations, leading her to ultimately face off against Risky in her hideout.
lead
The game became obscure due to its release coming a year after that of the Game Boy Advance.
lead

However, it received favorable reviews and has garnered recognition since its release, being included on multiple lists of best games on the platform, and being called a " cult classic " by some reviewers.
lead
It was re-released via the Nintendo 3DS Virtual Console in 2013, marking the first time the game was made available in Europe.
lead
A port for Nintendo Switch was released in April 2021, and for PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5 in June 2023.
Gameplay
Shantae must use these abilities to reach new areas or find hidden items.
Gameplay
During nighttime, players can collect hidden fireflies, with a reward available for collecting them all.
Gameplay

Other collectible creatures include Warp Squids, which are squid-shaped items hidden within dungeons, and which can be given to larger mother squids in each town in exchange for the ability to instantly warp there.
Setting and characters
With time, genies fell in love with humans and had children with them, half-genies with limited magical powers.
Plot
Risky Boots and her gang of Tinkerbat pirates attack Scuttle Town and steals a prototype steam engine from Mimic, the town's resident treasure hunter.
Plot
At the fourth dungeon, Shantae finds the last stone, but is ambushed at the exit by Risky, who steals the stones and escapes.
Plot

After, she is magically abducted to a place called the Genie Realm where the genies offer her a chance to remain with them as a reward for her courage, but at the price of never seeing her friends again.
Game development
The game was considered for development by WayForward as far back as 1997.
Game development

An archived version of the company's official website showcases a very different approach to the game, which was at the time considered for development on PC or PlayStation, in full 3D with traditionally animated characters moving in a 3D background.
Game development

In the first four months of development, the team created most of the animation, and Huey programmed an art-capturing tool that allowed to take full-colored animation frames, turn them into three-color chunks and reassemble the whole on the GBC's screen.
Publishing
The Game Boy Game Pak needed 4 megabytes of ROM and battery-backed RAM to work properly, making it expensive to produce.
Publishing
It is rumored that the game had only one run of 20–25,000 copies.
Music
In 2000, the sound was developed using the Musyx audio format, but WayForward chose to switch during development.
Music
The soundtrack featured about 20 songs at the time, and was composed by Jake Kaufman.
Music
Kaufman ultimately used the Paragon 5 GameBoy Tracker to create the music.
Music
Paragon 5's CEO, Paul Bragiel, served as music producer, and Stephane Hockenhull performed music replay.
Music
The soundtrack to the game was released in January 2019 by Fangamer in a red vinyl format, with a limited edition purple variant published by Limited Run Games.
Sales and analysis

Precise sales figures for the game have not been made public, but according to Bozon, it sold poorly; he said that he had heard that 20–25,000 copies of the game were produced, which did sell out, but that a second print run did not get made.
Sales and analysis
Matt Bozon has refused to blame Capcom, the publisher of the game, for responsibility in the game's failure.
Sales and analysis
This was despite Capcom holding it for 8 months after completion, with the game finally releasing when the Game Boy Advance was already in its first year of existence.
Sales and analysis

Bozon believed that from a creative standpoint, he never really settled on a target audience, with the character being "iconoclastic", "too sexy to be a kid's brand, and too girly for a male gamer brand".
Critical reception
Retrospective reviews were positive as well, with Kaes Delgrego and Corbie Dillard of Nintendo Life and Kyle MacGregor of Destructoid claiming the game to be a "cult classic".
Critical reception

A new 2013 review for the re-release of the game on the Nintendo 3DS Virtual Console by Mike Mason claimed that the "2D platformer is sprinkled with enough genie-magic to keep it fresh and interesting for a modern audience."
Critical reception
Game Informer ' s Ben Reeves called Shantae the 15th best Game Boy game and felt that it was overlooked.
Critical reception
Complex named it the 7th best GBC game in 2013, calling it a "solid platformer".
Critical reception
GamesRadar ranked it as the 8th best Game Boy game, saying that " Shantae' s filled with typical 2D platformer stuff but it’s all done remarkably well and with a visual flair the GBC rarely saw".
Critical reception
In 2018, the game was ranked as the 9th best GB/GBC game by French website Jeuxvideo.com, calling it an "excellent action-platforming game with superb art direction".
Critical reception

Because of the success of its sequels and its very positive critical reviews, as well as the short initial run of cartridges, Shantae has become one of the most sought-after and rare Game Boy Color games.
Sequels

On September 15, 2009, a sequel titled Shantae: Risky's Revenge was announced, and revealed as a downloadable DSiWare title on Nintendo of America's 2009 Holiday lineup, with a tentative 2009 Q4 release date.
Sequels
Details on the 3-part episodic sequels were revealed in the November 2009 issue of Nintendo Power.
Sequels
However, plans for the episodic release were cancelled, and the game was instead released as a stand-alone sequel for a title to be available on DSiWare on October 4, 2010.
Sequels
The game was later ported to iOS, Microsoft Windows and PlayStation 4.
Sequels
A third game, Shantae and the Pirate's Curse, was released on the Nintendo 3DS eShop on October 23, 2014.
Sequels
Later the game was also released on Wii U, Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 4, Xbox One and Amazon Fire TV.
Sequels
A fourth title, Shantae: Half-Genie Hero, was released for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 4, PlayStation Vita, Wii U, Xbox One and Nintendo Switch; it is the first HD game in the series.
Sequels
The game was successfully crowdfunded via Kickstarter and PayPal, receiving nearly $950,000, more than doubling its initial goal.
Sequels
A fifth game, Shantae and the Seven Sirens, was released for Apple Arcade in 2019, and for PC, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and Nintendo Switch in 2020.
Sequels
The previously canceled sequel, Risky Revolution, is set for release in 2025 as the sixth game in the series.
Re-releases
Shantae was digitally re-released by WayForward via the Nintendo 3DS Virtual Console on July 18, 2013.
Re-releases
In July 2020, Limited Run Games announced they would be producing a brief run of new Shantae cartridges for Game Boy Color, with pre-orders scheduled to begin the following September.
Re-releases

WayForward also announced that they would be releasing a port of the game for Nintendo Switch, both digitally and as a limited physical release from Limited Run, using the Carbon Engine, which is Limited Run's new emulation software engine for modern hardware.
Re-releases

The port, released on April 22, 2021, allows players to toggle the Game Boy Advance enhancements on and off; it also includes save state functionality, alternate display options, and an in-game art gallery.
Re-releases
Versions for PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5 were released on June 2, 2023.

pboy_metal_gear_sneaky.title: Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection
sents: lead
Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection is a video game compilation published by Konami.
lead
The compilation features ports of titles in the Metal Gear franchise of stealth games, released in commemoration of the series' 35th anniversary.
lead
1 was released for Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Windows, and Xbox Series X/S on October 24, 2023.
lead
More volumes will be announced and detailed in the future.
Games
1 presents five individual applications, each comprising one or two games and additional versions as well as its additional content.
Games
Metal Gear Solid and its two sequels each have their own application, while the MSX versions of Metal Gear and Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake are contained in one application.
Games

The Nintendo Entertainment System (NES) games Metal Gear (1987) and Snake's Revenge (1990) have their own application, labeled as "Bonus Content", including extra content such as the music player and graphic novels.
Games
Metal Gear Solid and its sequels can be purchased individually, with Metal Gear Solid bundling Metal Gear and Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake.
Games

Due to the original Metal Gear Solid being presented in a 4:3 aspect ratio, an assortment of wallpapers can be selected both from the main menu and during gameplay, as well as adjustments to the game's display position.
Games

The collection includes the ability to create virtual save data for other Konami PlayStation titles and virtually swap controller ports from Player 1 to Player 2, which are both relevant to the boss fight against Psycho Mantis.
Games

Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty (2001) and Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater (2004) are both direct conversions of their HD Edition remasters previously developed by Bluepoint Games and distributed as part of the Metal Gear Solid HD Collection (2011) compilation for PlayStation 3, PlayStation Vita and Xbox 360.
Games
Before release Konami announced that on PlayStation 5, Windows and Xbox Series X/S, all featured games are presented at a resolution of 1080p at a maximum performance of 60 frames-per-second (FPS).
Games
The Nintendo Switch version of the collection similarly retains a native 1080p resolution in TV Mode, but has a lower output of 720p in Handheld Mode, while both configurations run at 30 FPS.
Games
The Switch version's 30 FPS cap was noted as "bizarre" since the Shield version, which the Switch version is derived from, manages to run at 60 FPS using the same Tegra X1 chip.
Additional content

Remixes of the vocal tracks "The Best is Yet to Come" from Metal Gear Solid, "Can't Say Goodbye To Yesterday" from Sons of Liberty and the titular "Snake Eater" from Metal Gear Solid 3, was made available as pre-order bonuses.
Development

In November 2021, the digital downloads for Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty and Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater as well as the original Metal Gear Solid HD Collection were removed from digital storefronts, with Konami citing expired licenses as the reason.
Development
In July 2022, Konami announced their intentions to reinstate the games for the series' 35th anniversary.
Development

During the development of Metal Gear Solid Delta: Snake Eater, Konami began the development of the Master Collection series to make "the most complete collection that celebrates the 35th anniversary of the series, allowing fans to play the games as they were, as first released on the latest platforms."
Marketing and release
1 was announced for the PlayStation 5 during a PlayStation Showcase in May 2023, immediately after the reveal of Metal Gear Solid Delta: Snake Eater.
Marketing and release
In the original announcement, it was revealed to contain the first three Metal Gear Solid games.
Marketing and release

In June 2023, a Nintendo Direct revealed that the compilation would be released for Nintendo Switch, that it would include the Nintendo Entertainment System version of Metal Gear and its standalone sequel Snake's Revenge, and that it would include digital graphic novels for Metal Gear Solid and Metal Gear Solid 2.
Marketing and release

In August 2023, a digital release for PlayStation 4 was confirmed to be in development, and was later announced as releasing the same day as on other platforms, with PS4 players entitled to a free PS5 upgrade.
Marketing and release
1 released on October 24, 2023, alongside standalone versions of the three Metal Gear Solid games for $19.99 each.
Marketing and release
Buying the standalone version of Metal Gear Solid grants access to Metal Gear and Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake.
Marketing and release

The Nintendo Switch physical release in North America and Europe only includes Metal Gear for MSX2, Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake, Metal Gear for NES and Snake's Revenge on the Game Card, while the rest of the contents have to be separately downloaded and installed to the console.
Reception

The Nintendo Switch version of the compilation was scored the highest at 78/100 on review aggregator website Metacritic, while both the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S versions garnered a comparatively lower aggregate score of 74/100.

pba_pocket_critters_emerald.title: Pokémon Emerald
sents: lead
Pokémon Emerald Version is a 2004 role-playing video game developed by Game Freak and published by The Pokémon Company and Nintendo for the Game Boy Advance.
lead
It was first released in Japan in 2004, and was later released internationally in 2005.
lead
It is the third version after Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire and is the final game of the third generation of the Pokémon video game series.
lead
The gameplay and controls are largely the same as the previous games in the series; players control a Pokémon trainer from an overhead perspective.
lead
Along with Pokémon that debuted in Ruby and Sapphire, the game incorporates Pokémon from Pokémon Gold and Silver not featured in Ruby and Sapphire.
lead
Emerald ' s reception was generally positive upon release.
lead
Praise was given to the addition of the Battle Frontier and for fixing story elements.
Gameplay
Trainers send out the first Pokémon in their party and they take turns attacking where the first strike is determined usually by the speed of the two Pokémon.
Gameplay
When a Pokémon hits 0 hit points (HP), they faint, forcing the Pokémon's trainer to switch out.
Gameplay
Unlike Ruby and Sapphire which had the player fight two specific trainers, Emerald allowed for the player to have a 2-on-2 battle with two trainers both of whom they could usually battle separately.
Gameplay
Rare Pokémon that originated from earlier Pokémon games such as Mew, Lugia, and Ho-Oh were made available through an in-game event.
Setting and story
Along the way, they make two rivals: May or Brendan, the child of the Pokémon Professor Birch, and Wally, a timid child from Petalburg who the player assists in catching his first Pokémon, a Ralts.
Setting and story
Along their journey, they face both Team Magma and Team Aqua, who originally could only be faced in Ruby and Sapphire, respectively.
Setting and story
Between the player's visit to the seventh and eighth gyms, both teams summon their respectively-sought legendary Pokémon with mystical orbs stolen from Mt.
Development and promotion
It features compatibility with the Nintendo e-Reader and 83 cards launched for Emerald on October 7, 2004.
Development and promotion

The competition took place in seven areas across the United States and Canada, where 14 finalists, two from each area, competed in Seattle, Washington's Space Needle for a trip for two to the Pokémon Park in Nagoya, Japan.
Development and promotion
A limited edition Game Boy Advance SP was released by Nintendo which featured a silhouette of the Pokémon Rayquaza.
Development and promotion

Players who brought their Game Boy Advance with a copy of Emerald and a wireless adapter to Booth 2029 of the 2005 Comic-Con International were given an in-game item called the Mystic Ticket which allows players the opportunity to capture Lugia and Ho-oh.
Critical reception
Pokémon Emerald received generally positive reception and holds aggregate scores of 76/100 and 76.65% on Metacritic and GameRankings respectively.
Critical reception
1UP.com ' s Christian Nutt felt that it was the definitive version of Pokémon at the time yet was also a rehash.
Critical reception
Nintendo Life ' s Laurie Blake performed a retroactive review of Emerald; she felt that the Pokémon games have aged well but still feel like they did in 1996.
Critical reception
Fellow 1UP.com editor Kat Bailey included it in her list of remakes that "left the originals in the dust".
Sales
Emerald launched in the top spot in Japan with 791,000 copies sold in its first week and 372,000 copies sold in its first day.
Sales
It sold 1.4 million for the year and ranked behind Dragon Quest V: Hand of the Heavenly Bride, Pokémon FireRed and LeafGreen (combined), and Dragon Quest VIII: Journey of the Cursed King.
Sales
The list of the top 1000 best-selling video games in Japan for 2010 featured Emerald at 779 with 7,724 copies sold for a total of 1,916,505 sold since release.
Sales
More than 146,000 people pre-ordered copies of Emerald in the US.
Sales

Emerald launched in the United States at the number one position in May; it followed in June by falling to the number two spot below Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas on Xbox with 265,000 copies sold in that month.
Sales
It had sold 1.72 million copies worldwide by June 1, 2005.
Sales
It was the second best-selling game for the first half of 2005.
Sales
In a poll conducted by IGN, readers ranked Emerald as the most popular Game Boy Advance game for the 2005 holiday season.
Sales
It ranked second for the whole year of 2005 below Madden NFL 06.
Sales
By the end of 2005 it had sold 1.2 million in Europe and nearly 5 million worldwide.
Sales
To date it is one of the three best-selling Game Boy Advance games.
Sales
Its life-to-date sales totaled 6.32 million by the 2007 fiscal year.
Sales
In November 2005, Nintendo Power erroneously reported that "Total sales would exceed the value of an actual emerald the size of Neptune."

pba_pocket_critters_sapphire.title: Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire
sents: lead
Pokémon Omega Ruby and Pokémon Alpha Sapphire are 2014 remakes of the 2002 Game Boy Advance role-playing video games Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire, also including features from Pokémon Emerald.
lead
The games are part of the sixth generation of the Pokémon video game series, developed by Game Freak and published by The Pokémon Company and Nintendo for the Nintendo 3DS.
lead

Announced in May 2014, the games were released in Japan, North America and Australia on 21 November 2014, exactly twelve years after the original release date of Ruby and Sapphire, while the European release was the following week.
lead
Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire received generally positive reviews from critics.
lead
As of 31 March 2023, a combined total of 14.57 million copies have been sold worldwide, ranking them as the fourth-best-selling Nintendo 3DS titles of all time.
Gameplay
The games introduced a unique mechanic for Kyogre and Groudon dubbed "Primal Reversion", akin to the broader Mega Evolution feature.
Setting and story
Aside from the gameplay, 21 new Mega Evolutions were added since Pokémon X and Y, as well as "primal reversions" for Groudon and Kyogre, which function similarly.
Release

Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire were released in Japan, North America and Australia on 21 November 2014, exactly twelve years after the original release date of Ruby and Sapphire, while the European release was the following week.
Release
They are the third remake pairs in the franchise following Pokémon FireRed and LeafGreen for the Game Boy Advance in 2004 and Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver for the Nintendo DS in 2009.
Release

As with Pokémon X and Y, the games include all official translations, unlike previous generations where games contained only certain languages depending on the region or country they were originally distributed.
Reception
GameSpot ' s Peter Brown praised the 3D visuals and the super training mechanic, but believed the game failed to fully resolve general issues in the game formula.
Reception
IGN ' s Kallie Plagge also praised the game's 3D reinvention of Hoenn and online functionality.
Reception
At the 2014 Game Awards it was nominated for Best Remaster, but lost out to Grand Theft Auto V.
Sales
The games sold 3,040,000 copies in their first three days of sale.
Sales
Of the total sales, 1,534,593 copies were sold in Japan, the rest were sold in North America and Australia.
Sales
Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire had the biggest launch in the series history in the United Kingdom, beating the previous record held by Pokémon Black and White.
Sales
By the end of 2014, the games had sold 2.4 million copies in Japan.
Sales
As of 31 March 2023, a combined total of 14.57 million copies have been sold worldwide, ranking them as the fourth-best-selling Nintendo 3DS titles of all time.

pba_pocket_critters_firered.title: Pokémon FireRed and LeafGreen
sents: lead
Pokémon FireRed Version and Pokémon LeafGreen Version are 2004 remakes of the 1996 role-playing video games Pokémon Red and Blue.
lead
They were developed by Game Freak and published by The Pokémon Company and Nintendo for the Game Boy Advance.
lead
FireRed and LeafGreen were first released in Japan in January 2004 and in North America and Europe in September and October 2004.
lead
The games are part of the third generation of the Pokémon video game series and hold the distinction of being the first enhanced remakes of previous games within the franchise.
lead
As in previous games, the player controls their character from an overhead perspective and participates in turn-based battles.
lead
Throughout the games, the player captures and raises Pokémon for use in battle.
lead
Based in the Kanto region, new features include a contextual help menu and a new area (Sevii Islands) the player may access after defeating the Elite 4 and the champion.
lead
The games have compatibility with the Game Boy Advance Wireless Adapter, which originally came bundled with the games.
Gameplay
During a battle, the player may select a move for their Pokémon to perform, use an item, switch their active Pokémon, or attempt to flee (in wild battles only).
Gameplay
All Pokémon moves have power points (PP); when a Pokémon tries to perform a move while awake, the move's PP is reduced by 1.
Gameplay

While FireRed and LeafGreen are remakes of Red and Green (Pokémon Green was only released in Japan, whereas the international variant was Blue), they contain usability enhancements such as a contextual tutorial feature which allows players to look up data at any point in the game, by pressing the select button.
Gameplay
Players may also connect with Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire, as well as with Pokémon Colosseum, allowing them to obtain over 350 Pokémon.
Gameplay
FireRed and LeafGreen are also the first games in the series to be compatible with the Game Boy Advance Wireless Adapter, which comes prepackaged with the games.
Gameplay
The adapter can be plugged into the link port of the Game Boy Advance system and allows players within a radius of 30–50 feet (9.1–15.2 m) to wirelessly interact with each other.
Setting
Some areas are only accessible once players acquire a special item or one of their Pokémon learns a special ability.
Story
Profesor Samuel Oak, a famous Pokémon Researcher, explains to the player that such grass is often the habitat of wild Pokémon, and encountering them alone can be very dangerous.
Story
After the first time players defeat the Elite Four, one of the members, Lorelei, disappears.
Development
FireRed and LeafGreen were first announced in September 2003 as upcoming remakes of the original Pocket Monsters Red and Blue games that were released in Japan in 1996.
Development
The exclusive Japanese production run for FireRed and LeafGreen was limited to half a million copies, despite the success of Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire.
Development
IGN speculated that Nintendo was expecting less demand for the new games, or that it was limited by the production of the bundled wireless adapter.
Development
The North American versions of FireRed and LeafGreen were indirectly announced at DICE in 2004.
Music

A two-disc set of the music entitled GBA Pokémon FireRed & LeafGreen Super Complete was released, with the first disc featuring all the music used normally in-game, while the second disc featured bonus tracks based on and inspired by the music in the games.
Reception
Reviews of FireRed and LeafGreen were mostly positive, and the games currently hold an aggregate score of 81 percent on Metacritic.
Reception
Craig Harris of IGN gave the games an "Outstanding" 9.0/10 rating and praised the creators of the games for creating a game that "works extremely well for the handheld market.
Reception
Game Informer rated the games a "Very Good" 8/10 for being "a lot of fun", yet they saw the graphics as "utterly unremarkable" when compared to other handheld games.
Reception
The engrossingly simple gameplay combined with the more-strategic-than-they-first-appear battles was just too much to resist.
Sales

During its first week of release in Japan, FireRed and LeafGreen sold a combined total of 885,039 copies, which was less than the number sold by Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire in that time period, but IGN reasoned that the smaller sales were due to the new titles being remakes.
Sales
In the first half of August before FireRed and LeafGreen were released in the United States, the games received over 150,000 pre-orders, over twice the number Ruby and Sapphire received.
Sales

Nintendo's Senior Vice President of Marketing and Corporate Communication George Harrison remarked, "This pre-sell indicates more than twice the player interest!" Over one million copies of FireRed and LeafGreen were sold in the US less than one month after their release in that region.
Sales
As of March 31, 2008, the games had sold 11.82 million copies worldwide.

sents: lead
Pokémon Mystery Dungeon is a video game series spin-off from the main Pokémon series developed by Spike Chunsoft (formerly Chunsoft).
lead

The games feature the fictional creatures called Pokémon who have the ability to speak human language navigating through a randomly generated dungeon using turn-based moves, common to Mystery Dungeon games.
lead
As of March 2020, there have been eleven games across five platforms, as well as several manga adaptations and animated specials.
lead
These games are based in dungeons (“mystery dungeons”) where a floor map is randomly generated.
lead
In the dungeons, players fight other Pokémon while obtaining items and finding stairs to the next floor, exiting the dungeon after a fixed number of floors.
lead
Across all installments, the series has sold over 17.15 million copies.
Gameplay
The game starts with one partner Pokémon, but the player can recruit other Pokémon that they meet in the dungeon into their team soon after the first mission.
Development
One of the company's work was Tetris 2 + Bombliss, where Ishihara was the game's producer and met Koichi Nakamura, who was the game's director.
Development
During the development of Red and Blue Rescue Team, Kouji Maruta, one of the programmer for these two games, and contributed previously on EarthBound and Shiren the Wanderer 2: Oni Invasion!
Development
The game's success not only helped to give more popularity to the franchise, it also helped Chunsoft avoid bankruptcy.
Games
The games are developed by Spike Chunsoft, formerly Chunsoft before the merging in 2012, and published by Nintendo and The Pokémon Company.
Games

Games
Two years later, Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Explorers of Time and Explorers of Darkness for Nintendo DS were released in 2007 in Japan, then worldwide in 2008.
Games
Starting from Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Explorers of Sky in 2009, the sister game and enhanced remake of Explorers of Time and Darkness, the series would not be released in Taiwan and South Korea.
Games
Most retailers in Australia stocked UK-imported versions.
Games
As such, they are the first and only Pokémon Mystery Dungeon games to never be released overseas.

These games utilize the 3D models from Pokémon Rumble and My Pokémon Ranch, making them the first games to use models instead of 2D sprites.
Games
By using WiiConnect24, new missions are added to the game while the Wii is asleep, and players can share save data throughout all three games.
Games
In 2012, Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Gates to Infinity was released for the Nintendo 3DS in Japan, before being released worldwide in 2013.
Games
From there on, the series use purpose-made 3D models, as opposed to 2D sprites or 3D models from other spin-off titles.
Games
Pokémon Super Mystery Dungeon is the latest non-remake release in the series, released in 2015 on Nintendo 3DS, then in 2016 in PAL regions.
Games
Finally, Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Rescue Team DX is the latest title in the series, released on Nintendo Switch in 2020.
