In its year of release in Japan, Persona sold 391,556 units, reaching number 21 in the 100 best-selling games of that year.
Reception
The PSP port of the game was also highly successful: while Atlus estimated sales of 50,000 and 35,000 units in Japan and North America, respectively, actual sales reached 160,000 and 49,000 units.
Reception

GameSpot ' s Lark Anderson was more critical than most, praising the story and improved localization, but finding the combat, navigation and graphics fairly dated compared to both recent and contemporary RPGs.
Reception
IGN's Sam Bishop shared critiques about the graphics with other reviewers, but enjoyed most other parts of the game, and particularly appreciated the inclusion of the Snow Queen route.
Legacy
Revelations: Persona was successful enough to establish the Persona series in North America and become a cult classic.
Legacy
Persona 2: Innocent Sin, which was released in 1999 and involved many of the same staff.
Legacy
Originally serialized in 1996, it was later reissued in 2009.
Legacy
In 2006, Atlus and mobile company Bbmf released a mobile spin-off game, Megami Ibunroku Persona: Ikū no Tō-hen.
Legacy
The unexpected success of the PSP port of Persona led to the development of enhanced remakes for both Innocent Sin and its sequel, Persona 2: Eternal Punishment.

pst_personna_2_eternal_punishmen.title: Persona 2: Eternal Punishment
sents: lead
Persona 2: Eternal Punishment is a 2000 role-playing video game by Atlus for the PlayStation.
lead
It is chronologically the third installment in the Persona series, a subseries of the Megami Tensei franchise.
lead
The game was later remade by Atlus for the PlayStation Portable.
lead
This version, released in Japan in 2012, did not receive an overseas release.
lead
In response to this, the PlayStation version was released on PlayStation Network in 2013.
lead
Eternal Punishment takes place in the fictional Japanese city of Sumaru, and is a direct sequel to Persona 2: Innocent Sin.
lead

Taking place a few months after Innocent Sin, the game follows reporter Maya Amano as she investigates the Joker Curse, a malign phenomenon where people's wishes and rumors are coming true and causing chaos.
lead
During her investigations, she and others who join her gain the ability to summon Personas, personified aspects of their personalities.
Gameplay
Persona 2: Eternal Punishment is a role-playing game where the player takes control of a group of characters exploring the fictional city of Sumaru.
Gameplay
While a Persona is originally quite weak, if it is used enough, it will achieve a higher rank, with Rank 8 being the highest possible.
Setting and characters

Set a few months after the ending of Persona 2: Innocent Sin, Eternal Punishment takes place in 1999 in Sumaru, a fictional seaside city in Japan with a population of 1.28 million, its own television stations, and a structure left over from its foundations during the Warring States period.
Setting and characters
During the events of Innocent Sin, Nyarlathotep influenced events in his favor and all the world except Sumaru City was destroyed.
Plot
The party eventually learn that Tatsuzou and a secret organization he leads, the New World Order, are manipulating Sumaru's government, corporations, and media for his own ends.
Plot
The only way to stop the plan's fulfillment is defeating the Order.
Plot

Tatsuya refused to forget the events of the Other Side, creating a dangerous loophole: if all the other members of the original group could be forced to remember, the Other Side would be brought back into existence, destroying the present reality.
Development
One of the biggest concerns when making Eternal Punishment was how much the development staff wanted to include, which went well beyond their original plans.
Development
The character of Nyarlathotep, who had made a cameo appearance as a Persona in the original game, was inspired by the character of the same name from H.
Port and localization
Eternal Punishment was first announced in April at the 2000 Tokyo Game Show.
Port and localization
The localization was released on December 22, 2000.
Port and localization
Eternal Punishment received a limited reprint exclusive to Amazon.com in 2008 to celebrate the release of Persona 4.
Port and localization
The team carried over most of the features implemented Innocent Sin ' s remake while further simplifying and streamlining the mechanics, aiming for a "culmination" to Persona 2 as a whole.
Port and localization
Game Informer included the game on its list of "RPGs Released Late In The PSP's Life Cycle", games that were likely never to see a release due to the flagging western PSP market.
Port and localization
In response to the decision not to localize the remake, the original version was released on PlayStation Network in 2013.
Port and localization
Intended to be playable on PSP, PlayStation Vita and PlayStation 3, a fault at release meant only the PS3 version was playable, which was fixed after players complained about it.
Port and localization
An English fan translation of the remake was released in July 2022.
Music
Together with Innocent Sin, Eternal Punishment is one of the first entries in the Megami Tensei series to feature voice acting.
Music

For Kitajoh, one of the most notable arrangements he did was for "Maya's Theme": Meguro, who had previously remixed this track for Persona 3: FES, asked for a remix with a faster tempo and hard rock elements incorporated.
Reception
During its first week of release in Japan, Eternal Punishment reached the top of Japanese sales charts, selling 106,563 copies.
Reception
The following week, the game was still in the top five, selling a further 16,333 and bringing sales to 122,896.
Reception
By the end of the year, it ranked at #60 in Japan's best-selling titles of the year, with final sales totaling 200,103 units.
Reception
The PSP remake debuted at #3 in Japanese sales charts, selling 24,547 copies.
Reception
The following week, it sold a further 4,885, but had dropped to #20.
Reception

By October 2012, as stated in Index Holding 's announced sales data, the game had sold just 60,000 copies, putting it well behind other Atlus titles such as Etrian Odyssey IV: Legends of the Titan for the Nintendo 3DS and Persona 4 Golden for the Vita.
Reception

The magazine's later review of the remake was also fairly positive, finding the atmosphere somber and the battles entertaining, stating that the reviewers appreciated being able to play both parts of Persona 2 on PSP.
Legacy

The next title in the series, Persona 3 for the PlayStation 2, was released in 2006; unlike Eternal Punishment, it was released with the Shin Megami Tensei franchise moniker in non-Japan regions, a branding that would continue for the Persona series until Persona 5 in 2017.
Legacy
In 2009, Atlus and Bbmf developed and published a mobile version of the game titled Persona 2: Eternal Punishment – Infinity Mask (ペルソナ2 罰 インフィニティマスク, Perusona Tsū: Batsu Infiniti Masuku).

pst_personna_2_innocent_sin.title: Persona 2: Innocent Sin
sents: lead
Persona 2: Innocent Sin is a 1999 role-playing video game by Atlus for the PlayStation.
lead
It is the second entry in the Persona series, itself a subseries of the Megami Tensei franchise, and acts as a sequel to the original Persona.
lead
The game was re-released in 2011 for the PlayStation Portable.
lead
The original version was not localized for western territories; however, the PSP version was released in North America and Europe under the title Shin Megami Tensei: Persona 2 – Innocent Sin.
lead
Innocent Sin takes place in the fictional Sumaru City, focusing on a group of high school students from Seven Sisters High School.
lead
The protagonist, Tatsuya Suou, and a group of friends must confront a villainous figure called Joker, who is causing the spread of reality-warping rumors through the city.
lead
The group are aided in their quest by their Personas, personified aspects of their personalities.
lead

The gameplay features turn-based battle gameplay, where characters use their Personas in battle against demons, and a separate Rumor system, where rumors spread around the city can influence events in the characters' favor.
Gameplay
Persona 2: Innocent Sin is a role-playing game where the player takes control of a group of high school students as they explore the fictional city of Sumaru.
Gameplay
While a Persona is originally quite weak, if it is used enough, it will achieve a higher rank.
Gameplay
During battles, players can converse with most enemies: depending on which character talks with which enemy, they will trigger a different response.
Setting and characters
Innocent Sin takes place in 1999 in Sumaru (珠閒瑠), a fictional seaside city in Japan with a population over 1.28 million.
Setting and characters
Most of the protagonists come from two high schools in Sumaru: Seven Sisters (七姉妹学園), a prestigious school which the protagonist attends, and the less-prestigious Kasugayama (春日山).
Plot
In a tragic twist of fate, the deranged Tatsuya Sudou set fire to the shrine, and it was only Maya awakening to her Persona that saved her from death.
Plot

Confronting the Joker and the final member of the Circle, Jun's estranged mother Junko, they and the Circle are attacked by group of rumor-generated Nazis called the Last Battalion, led by a resurrected " Fuhrer ".
Plot

With the Masked Circle and the Last Battalion waging war with each other, the party decide to return the city to normal by removing the five elemental crystal skulls being fought over by the two factions, then confront the Ideal Father.
Plot

After Nyarlathotep and Okamura leave, Philemon tells the remaining group that they can reverse Nyarlathotep's work by willing the erasure of the day the five first met as children from existence: in exchange, they must give up their shared memories.
Development

From a technical standpoint, the game not only changed to an overhead view from the first Persona ' s mixture of overhead and first person navigation, but also made improvements to elements that were criticized in Persona, such as load times and save point frequency.
Development
To separate the Persona series from the Megami Tensei series, the first game's banner title Megami Ibunroku was dropped.
Development

Another key element was the "power of Kotodama ", the Japanese belief that words can influence the physical and spiritual world, with this power manifesting in the world of Persona 2 through the spreading of rumors.
Development
The character of Nyarlathotep, who had made a cameo appearance as a Persona in the original game, was inspired by the character of the same name from H.
Port and localization

Later, it was stated by Atlus staff that the main reason for this choice was a shortage of staff and resources, as most of the team needed to localize Innocent Sin were already working on its sequel Eternal Punishment, though the localization team did attempt to change this decision.
Port and localization
Despite this, it was reported in 2001 that there was still a chance of Innocent Sin being localized, with its release depending on whether Eternal Punishment was successful in North America.
Port and localization
A remake of Innocent Sin for the PlayStation Portable was announced by Famitsu in 2010.
Port and localization
A new opening movie was produced by animation studio Satelight, who had become famous in Japan through their work on Macross Frontier and Basquash!.
Port and localization

While most game openings were intended as a simple introduction, the team wanted this one to be about the re-imagination the game had undergone, so they decided to have an experienced outside studio work on it rather than internal staff.
Port and localization
One of the biggest challenges while creating the movie was remaining faithful to Kaneko's character artwork while establishing its own look and style.
Port and localization
For the remake, the gameplay was adjusted to resemble its sequel, along with adjusting it to a 16:9 screen ratio from the original 4:3, and interface adjustments for ease of play.
Port and localization
Until this point, Innocent Sin was the only Persona game not to be released overseas.
Music
Tsuchiya found working on the title difficult, retrospectively calling it his most difficult task until his work on Shin Megami Tensei IV.
Music
Innocent Sin was one of the first Megami Tensei titles to feature voice acting.
Music
The amount of music that needed remixing was very large, consisting of over 100 tracks.
Reception
In its year of release, Innocent Sin reached #62 in the Japanese sales charts, selling 274,798 copies.
Reception
The PSP remake reached #6 in the Japanese sales chart during its first week of release, selling 62,721 units.
Reception
It dropped to #11 by the following week, selling a further 10,400 units.
Reception
By October 2011, the game had sold 110,000 units in Japan, placing among Atlus' best-selling titles for that year.
Reception
During its first week on sale in North America, it reached second place in the PSP sales charts.
Reception
As a character, Tatsuya Suou has been positively received by critics and fans across his two major appearances in the Persona 2 duology.
Reception
The gameplay was praised by Bartholow, calling the Persona system "Surprisingly simple and well balanced", and admired the game's polish despite its limited use of the PlayStation hardware.
Legacy
Localized for the west, Eternal Punishment was released in 2000 in Japan and North America.
Legacy
In 2007, Atlus and Bbmf created and published a mobile version of Innocent Sin.
Legacy
Titled Persona 2: Innocent Sin – Lost Memories, it carried over the crucial systems of Innocent Sin, including the Persona and Rumor systems, while tailoring them for a mobile format.

pst_suiko_saga.title: Suikoden (video game)

Developer(s): Konami Computer Entertainment Tokyo (PS) System Sacom (PC) Konami Computer Entertainment Sapporo (Saturn)
Composer(s): Miki Higashino Tappy Iwase Hiroshi Tamawari Hirofumi Taniguchi Mayuko Kageshita

sents: lead
Suikoden (Japanese: 幻想水滸伝, Hepburn: Gensō Suikoden,) is a role-playing video game published by Konami.
lead
It is the first installment of the Suikoden series.
lead
Developed by Konami Computer Entertainment Tokyo, it was released initially in 1995 for the PlayStation in Japan.
lead
A North American release followed one year later, and a mainland European release came the following April.
lead
The game was also released for Windows and Sega Saturn in 1998, but only in Japan.
lead
The game centers on the political struggles of the Scarlet Moon Empire.
lead

The player controls a Scarlet Moon Empire general's son, who is destined to seek out 108 warriors (referred to as the 108 Stars of Destiny) in order to revolt against the corrupt sovereign state and bring peace to a war-torn land.
lead

The game is loosely based on the Chinese novel Water Margin, and features a vast array of characters both controllable and not, with over ninety characters usable in combat and many more able to help or hinder the hero in a variety of ways.
Gameplay
Some characters can only be recruited if the party has reached a certain experience level or found a special item.
Gameplay
Weapons are unique to each character and require sharpening in towns that have blacksmiths.
Gameplay
There are no weapon shops in Suikoden and equipment shopping is limited to armour and items.
Gameplay
For instance, a character with four level 1 spell slots and a Water Rune could cast "Kindness Drops" (the level 1 Water Rune spell) four times.
Gameplay
Other runes offer different benefits such as allowing a character to deal double damage at the cost of a 50% reduction in defence.
Gameplay
Most runes can only be used in a limited capacity.
Plot

Through Ted, who is left hurt by a top servant of the king's, he comes into possession of the Rune of Life and Death (also known as the Soul Eater), one of 27 True Runes that govern various aspects of the world.
Plot

In his short time there, the hero is only convinced of the need to struggle against the Empire when the hideout is attacked and sacked by Imperial forces, who kill Odessa after she tries to protect an innocent child.
Characters
Suikoden boasts over 108 allied characters and numerous enemies and neutral characters.
Audio
The soundtrack was published by King Records and released in Japan on April 5, 1996.
Audio
The soundtrack contained 2 discs and a total of 48 tracks.
Reception
It has averaged a score of 82% on GameRankings culled from 14 reviews.
Reception

A reviewer for Next Generation called it "one of the most addictive RPGs to come along." He particularly praised the look of the combat engine, the strategic elements of the war battles, and the lack of a resurrection mechanic.
Reception
IGN claimed the game was "one of the best RPGs ever made", stating that although its story is simple, the background visuals and music are beautiful and fantastic, and it never becomes boring.
Reception

Peter Tieryas of Kotaku described the narrative as telling "a sweeping tale about justice, corruption, and humanity in a way few games have." Game Informer ranked it the 82nd best game ever made in its 100th issue in 2001.
Legacy
Its direct sequel was Suikoden II, which first released in 1998.
Legacy
He said the limited choices in Suikoden inspired him to expand on the idea with more meaningful choices, with the development of Deus Ex.

pst_suiko_saga_iii.title: Suikoden III

Composer(s): Michiru Yamane Takashi Yoshida Masahiko Kimura

sents: lead

Suikoden III (Japanese: 幻想水滸伝III, Hepburn: Gensō Suikoden Surī) is a role-playing video game developed by Konami Computer Entertainment Tokyo and published by Konami for the PlayStation 2 video game console, and the third installment in the Suikoden video game series.
lead
It was released in 2002 in Japan and North America, with a manga adaption published in 2004.
Mechanics

The game's story is presented through the "Trinity Sight System"; rather than having only one "hero", the plot is explored through three different viewpoints, allowing events to be seen from multiple sides.
Gameplay

Unlike Suikoden II and Suikoden V, Suikoden III has no "time limits" for character recruitment; assuming certain plot decisions are made "correctly," it is always possible to recruit all 108 Stars of Destiny.
Gameplay
Parties may consist of up to 6 characters who participate in combat and one "support" character who adds a special skill to the party, such as minor healing after battle.
Gameplay
If all 6 characters lose all their hit points (and are thus incapacitated), it is game over and the player must restart.
Gameplay

Characters have a certain number of spell usages per "spell level;" for instance, a character with 4 level 1 spell slots and a Water Rune could cast "Kindness Drops" (the level 1 Water Rune spell) 4 times.
Gameplay
For example, some Fire rune effects that only struck enemies in earlier Suikoden games now strike a generalized area, meaning they could affect allies who moved in too close.
Setting
Suikoden III is set in IS 475, roughly 16 in-game years after the events of Suikoden II.
Setting
In turn, all power from individual carved runes ultimately descends from the 27 True Runes, which created the world in Suikoden' s mythology.
Setting
Around 50 years prior to the start of Suikoden III, Harmonia attempted to extend its control over the Grasslands, and eventually invaded.
Hugo's point of view
The visit goes wrong, and Hugo is forced to flee back to Karaya, only to find it in flames.
Geddoe's point of view
Geddoe is in truth the bearer of the True Lightning Rune and was a personal companion of the Flame Champion from 50 years ago.
Turning point
At the end of each character's Chapter 3, they meet at the Flame Champion's hideout.
Turning point
Up until the end of Chapter 3, it is assumed by Hugo that the Flame Champion was still alive and would now join the group.
Chapters 4 and 5
At the onset of Chapter 4, the Harmonian army attacks in force.
Chapters 4 and 5

In Chapter 5, Luc's political scheme evaporates as he engages in his real plan- to steal all the elemental True Runes himself, and use their combined power to destroy his own True Rune that has dominated his destiny.
Other views

If the Thomas chapters are not completed by the time the third chapter for each other character has completed, they become unavailable, and Thomas and his acquaintances join the Stars of Destiny in Chapter 4.
Other views
If all 108 Stars of Destiny are recruited before the end of the game, then Luc's scenario may be seen, showing his band's plotting and scheming throughout the game.
Development
Suikoden III was developed by the same team as Suikoden II, for the most part.
Development
In June 2002, just a month before its release, some of Suikoden III 's team left Konami, including series creator Yoshitaka Murayama.
Soundtrack
The soundtrack was released on 2 CDs on July 24, 2002 as Genso Suikoden III Original Soundtrack.
Soundtrack

Miki Higashino, who had composed the main Suikoden themes and most of the music in the first two games, did not participate in the soundtrack, which explains the noticeable difference in style from the earlier soundtracks.
Soundtrack
On September 11, 2002, Genso Suikoden III Collection ~Rustling Wind~ was released, featuring 10 tracks from the game with new arrangements.
Sales
By the end of 2002, 377,729 copies of Suikoden III were sold in Japan.
Sales
Konami's policy at that time was that all PAL games had to be fully translated to the respective languages and that only releasing the game in English was not an option.
Sales

lead

In a later interview, Honeywood stated that the biggest issue was with the multiple religious references, and the concept at the end of "killing God", which needed to be adjusted so that it remained faithful to the original premise while stepping around some content that might offend.

lead

lead

lead

lead

The narrative deals with the themes of a rebellion against an immoral military dictatorship, pursuit of a magical arms race, use of chemical weapons in warfare, depictions of violent and apocalyptic confrontations, several personal redemption arcs, teenage pregnancy, and the renewal of hope and life itself.
lead
Final Fantasy VI received widespread critical acclaim, particularly for its graphics, soundtrack, story, characters, setting, and mature themes, and won numerous awards.
lead
It is widely considered to be one of the greatest video games ever made, and is often cited as a watershed title for the role-playing genre.
lead

The only notable changes to gameplay (in addition to loading times not present in the cartridge versions) involve the correction of a few software bugs from the original and the addition of a new "memo save" feature, allowing players to quickly save their progress to the PlayStation's RAM.

The port was re-released in December 2012 as part of the Final Fantasy 25th Anniversary Ultimate Box package in Japan.
PlayStation
Final Fantasy VI was re-released as a PSone Classic in 2011: in Japan on April 20, in PAL territories on June 2 and in North America on December 6.
PlayStation
The "Pixel Remaster" series version of Final Fantasy VI was released for PlayStation 4 in April 2023.
Nintendo consoles
It was released in Japan by Square Enix on November 30, 2006, with Nintendo handling publishing in North America on February 5, 2007, and in Europe on July 6.
Nintendo consoles
It was the last game to be released on the Game Boy Advance in Asia, as well as the last one to be published by Nintendo on the system.
Nintendo consoles
The original Super Famicom version was released for the Wii Virtual Console in Japan on March 15, 2011, in PAL territories (Europe and Australia) on March 18, and in North America on June 30.
Nintendo consoles
Square Enix released the Game Boy Advance version on the Wii U Virtual Console in Japan in December 2015.
Nintendo consoles
Nintendo re-released Final Fantasy VI worldwide in September 2017 as part of the company's Super NES/Super Famicom Classic Edition.
Nintendo consoles
The "Pixel Remaster" series version of Final Fantasy VI was released worldwide for Nintendo Switch in April 2023.
Mobile platforms and PC
A Windows PC port, itself a port of the Android version, was released for Windows PC via Steam on December 16, 2015.
Mobile platforms and PC
Another port from the "Pixel Remaster" line was released on Steam on February 23, 2022.
Mobile platforms and PC
The "Pixel Remaster" series features new 16-bit sprites, new soundtracks, and a return to the game's originally released content.
Contemporary
In mid-1994, Square's publicity department reported that the game had sold 2.55 million copies in Japan, where it became the best-selling video game of 1994.
Contemporary
In the United States, where it went on sale in the last quarter of 1994, it was the top-selling Super NES game in October and became the year's eighth best-selling Super NES cartridge.

As of March 2003, the game had shipped 3.48 million copies worldwide, with 2.62 million of those copies being shipped in Japan and 860,000 abroad.
