After a long period of hiatus, the film was re-announced in 2014, this time produced by Samuel Hadida, and was set to begin production after the completion and release of Fatal Frame: Maiden of Black Water.

pst2_rule_of_roze.title: Rule of Rose
sents: lead
Rule of Rose is a survival horror video game developed by Punchline for the PlayStation 2.
lead

Set in England in 1930, the plot revolves around a nineteen-year-old woman named Jennifer, who becomes trapped in a world ruled by young girls who have established a class hierarchy called the Red Crayon Aristocrats.
lead
It was first released in 2006 by Sony Computer Entertainment in Japan.
lead

After Sony Computer Entertainment's American and European branch did not express interest in localizing the title, it was published later that year by Atlus USA in North America and by 505 Games in Europe.
lead
Development on Rule of Rose began after Punchline was asked by Sony Computer Entertainment to make a horror game.
lead
Punchline wanted to develop a "new type of horror game" with an emphasis on psychological horror.
lead
This decision led to the concept of childhood, specifically the "mysterious and misunderstood" nature of young girls.
lead
The team drew inspiration from the classic Brothers Grimm fairy tales for the narrative, and the Silent Hill series for graphics and art style.
Gameplay
Most health restoratives and all tradable items are hidden and must be uncovered by Brown, though the player can choose to avoid searching for these items to progress quickly.
Gameplay
Other items such as marbles and ribbons have no immediate use, but may be traded with non-playable characters in order to obtain food, rare items, and weapons.
Gameplay
The game is largely linear and the player cannot affect the story through their actions, although they are rewarded for exploration with secret items, additional details and combat upgrades.
Plot
On a late night bus ride, 19-year-old Jennifer is given an unfinished storybook by a mysterious boy, but he runs away before she can return it.
Plot

As the newest and therefore the lowest ranking member of the Aristocracy, Jennifer frequently faces punishment for incidents caused by higher-ranking members, but manages to rescue a yellow Labrador from the other orphans, who she names Brown and takes with her.
Plot
Back on the airship, the club is in a state of emergency trying to find the stuffed bear, which has been presumed stolen.
Plot
Amanda is revealed to be the thief, but she betrays and frames Jennifer as having stolen the bear in order to gain a higher rank in the club.
Plot
Wendy gives Jennifer the gun she had stolen earlier in order to stop Stray Dog, and is then killed by Gregory.
Development
The company Punchline, which had previously developed the video game Chulip, developed Rule of Rose for the PlayStation 2.
Development

Though the game has garnered comparisons with William Golding 's 1954 allegorical novel Lord of the Flies, the developers did not draw inspiration from it, instead focusing on the "mysterious and misunderstood" nature of girls.
Development
The story formed through trial and error as the developers figured out how to create a sense of fear, ultimately adding the children's secret society, the Red Crayon Aristocrats.
Development
A 6-track promotional soundtrack CD was produced by Atlus, which was issued to customers from certain retailers when Rule of Rose was pre-ordered.
Controversy

At the time, Rule of Rose had already been rated by various video game advisory boards as suitable for an older teenage audience: in Japan, it was rated 15+; in the majority of Europe, 16+; and in North America, 17+.
Controversy

At this time, the game had not yet been released in Europe; the public officials suggesting that Rule of Rose be banned had not actually played the game, but had only read about its alleged content or watched the trailer.
Controversy
The Video Standards Council, the British body which had granted the title its 16+ PEGI rating, defended their decision.
Controversy
And the most violent scene does indeed see one of the young girls scare Jennifer with a rat on a stick.
Reception
IGN listed Rule of Rose as one of the worst horror games created after 2000.
Reception
Because of the limited number of copies published, Rule of Rose has garnered a reputation as one of the more expensive video games to buy second-hand.
Future
In 2021, Tokyo indie game developer Onion Games expressed interest in remastering Rule of Rose.
Future

Although they "can't guarantee that any of these initiatives will have more than a 1% chance of happening", they would like to give it a try after remastering a previous title for the Nintendo Switch called Moon.

pst2_haunting_grounds.title: Haunting Ground
sents: lead
Haunting Ground is a survival horror video game developed and published by Capcom for the PlayStation 2 in 2005.
lead
The story follows Fiona Belli, a young woman who wakes up in the dungeon of a castle after being involved in a car accident.
lead
She quickly befriends a White Shepherd, Hewie, and begins to explore the castle with his aid to seek a means of escape and unravel the mysteries of it and its inhabitants.
lead
The game shares many similarities with Capcom's earlier survival horror title Clock Tower 3, and has been described as a spiritual successor to the Clock Tower series.
lead
The player controls Fiona as she explores the environment, evades and hides from enemy pursuers, and occasionally fights against the castle's inhabitants.
lead
Sometimes Fiona will panic when in danger, in which case she begins to run on her own and the player loses some control.
lead
Hewie is a central part to the gameplay, and accompanies Fiona throughout the game.
lead
He can be given orders to explore the environment, attack enemies, and otherwise aid in Fiona's survival.
Gameplay
Haunting Ground is a survival horror game with similar gameplay elements to Clock Tower 3 (2002).
Gameplay
Other areas act as retaliation points that allow Fiona to use her environment to counterattack against her enemy, although some of these locations can only be used once.
Plot
Fiona Belli is an 18-year-old woman who recently moved to college.
Plot
While visiting her parents, Ugo and Ayla, the family is involved in a car accident, and Fiona alone awakens in a cage in the dungeon of a castle.
Plot
The first enemy Fiona encounters is Debilitas, a large, mentally disabled groundskeeper who thinks of Fiona as one of his dolls.
Plot
For the majority of the game, Riccardo keeps his face hidden under a hood.
Plot
Fiona first meets him as an old, crippled man.
Development and release
Rather than streaming audio files, the music for Haunting Ground was generated by using the PS2's built-in sounds.
Development and release
Capcom debuted Haunting Ground under its Japanese title Demento at the Tokyo Game Show in September 2004.
Development and release
The game was released in Japan on April 21, 2005, and later in PAL territories on April 29, and in North America on May 10.
Development and release
Critics described the game as a spiritual successor to the Clock Tower series, although it has never been officially declared as such.
Development and release
In July 2012, Haunting Ground appeared to be slated for a PlayStation 3 re-release as a "PS2 Classic", having been rated by the ESRB with Sony Computer Entertainment named as the publisher.
Development and release
It was re-released for the PlayStation 3 via the PlayStation Store exclusively in Japan in April 2015.
Reception
Critics were quick to compare it to the Clock Tower series, specifically its 2002 installment, Clock Tower 3 (2002).
Reception
The staff at 1UP.com described the environments as "some of the most detailed, lavish 3D environments Capcom has ever produced".
Reception
Kill Screen 's Astrid Budgor compared Haunting Ground's "psychological landscape" to Dario Argento's film Suspiria (1977) and also highlighted its grotesque expressionism.
Reception

The staff at 1UP.com felt the game was dated when compared with the recently released Resident Evil 4 (2005), but said: " Haunting Ground isn't without merit, it's just that the merits are buried deep in an occasionally thrilling, mostly 'been there, done that' game of indistinct origin".
Reception
Alexander ultimately felt Haunting Ground to be a "perfect illustration of how sexuality can be used to great effect".
Legacy
The player is never a spectator, nor do they take on the embodiment of Fiona, but float between these states of involvement.
Legacy
Capcom Card Fighters DS (2006), and as a costume for Cammy in Street Fighter V (2016).

pst2_silent_hull_2.title: Silent Hill 2

Genre: video game soundtrack, industrial, trip hop, dark ambient, alternative rock
Label: King Records (original release) Mondo (vinyl rerelease)

sents: lead
Silent Hill 2 is a 2001 survival horror game developed by Team Silent, a group in Konami Computer Entertainment Tokyo, and published by Konami.
lead
The game was released from September to November, originally for the PlayStation 2.
lead
The second installment in the Silent Hill series, Silent Hill 2 centers on James Sunderland, a widower who journeys to the town of Silent Hill after receiving a letter from his dead wife.
lead
An extended version containing a bonus scenario, Born from a Wish, and other additions was published for Xbox in December of the same year.
lead
In 2002, it was ported to Microsoft Windows and re-released for the PlayStation 2 as a Greatest Hits version, which includes all bonus content from the Xbox port.
lead
A remastered high-definition version was released for the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in 2012 as part of the Silent Hill HD Collection.
lead
Development of Silent Hill 2 began in June 1999, soon after Silent Hill had been completed.
lead
In contrast with the previous title, whose narrative concerned cult activity, Silent Hill 2 focuses directly on the psychology of its characters.
Gameplay
The objective of Silent Hill 2 is to guide the player character, James Sunderland, through the monster-filled town of Silent Hill as he searches for his deceased wife.
Gameplay

The default control for Silent Hill 2 has James moving in the direction that he is facing when the player tilts the analog stick upwards, although players can choose a more traditional control scheme.
Gameplay
Silent Hill 2 does not use a heads-up display; to check James' health, location, and items, the player must enter the pause-game menu to review his status.
Gameplay
Throughout the game, James collects maps, which can only be read if there is sufficient light or when his flashlight is on.
Gameplay
Similar to the first game, the player can choose to turn off the radio if they want.
Setting
While not focusing on the characters and plot threads of the first Silent Hill game, Silent Hill 2 takes place in the series' namesake town, located in Maine.
Setting
Silent Hill 2 is set in another area of the town, and explores some of Silent Hill's backstory.
Letter from Silent Heaven
Maria claims that she has never met or seen Mary, and because she is frightened by the monsters, James allows her to follow him.
Letter from Silent Heaven
Silent Hill 2 features six endings; Konami has kept their canonicity ambiguous.
Letter from Silent Heaven
In "Leave", James has one last meeting with Mary, reads her letter, and leaves the town with Laura.
Born from a Wish
Ernest refuses to let Maria into the room he is in and will only talk to her through its closed door.
Themes and analysis
Other noticeable themes in Silent Hill 2 are mental illness, lust, love and abuse, including an exploration of how it affects people.
Influences and design
Development of Silent Hill 2 began in June 1999, directly after the completion of its predecessor.
Influences and design

The story was conceived by CGI director Takayoshi Sato, who based it on Russian author Fyodor Dostoevsky 's novel Crime and Punishment (1866), with individual members of the team collaborating on the actual scenario.
Influences and design
Around the time Silent Hill 2 was in production, the average budget for video game production has been estimated to be around US$7–10 million by Sato.
Influences and design
As it was unable to gather information on the then-unannounced GameCube and Xbox consoles, they began production of the game for the PlayStation 2.
Influences and design
Producer Akihiro Imamura stated that the decision was also influenced by "a wish from the business section that we move rapidly on the PS2.
Influences and design
Imamura read all comments about the original game and kept them in mind while working on Silent Hill 2.
Influences and design
Developed at the same time, the PlayStation 2 version of Silent Hill 2 and its Xbox port debuted at the March 2001 Tokyo Game Show to positive reactions.
Influences and design
Silent Hill 2 shared the same atmosphere of psychological horror as the first Silent Hill game.
Influences and design
As the developers already had a rough sense of the game's environment, they focused on its plot first, in contrast to the process used with the first game.
Influences and design
The PlayStation 2 hardware allowed the developers to create improved fog and shadow special effects.
Influences and design
The team wanted Silent Hill 2 ' s protagonist to "reflect evil", against which the protagonist of the first game battles.
Influences and design
Early in the project, they studied the 1996 video game Tomb Raider ' s creation of 3D environments.
Influences and design
Other influences on the game included the 1992 survival horror video game Alone in the Dark, the first Silent Hill game, and Japanese comics by Daijiro Morohoshi and Junji Ito.
Influences and design
Masahiro Ito designed the monsters in Silent Hill 2; "soured flesh" was the concept behind their appearance.
Influences and design
For the most part, the monsters reflect the protagonist's subconscious.
Influences and design
Two exceptions to this theme are the "Abstract Daddy", a reflection of Angela's subconscious and memories, and the "Creepers", which are also seen in the first game.
Influences and design
Silent Hill 2 also incorporates some references to real-life events.
Influences and design

In the original scenario, the developers designed Maria and James with dual personalities: Maria's other personality was "Mary", a reference to Mary Jane Kelly, Jack the Ripper 's last victim, while James' was "Joseph", a reference to one of the Jack the Ripper suspects.
Influences and design
Eddie Dombrowski's name was taken from actor Eddie Murphy during the beginning phases of production when Eddie was originally designed with a pleasantly optimistic personality.
Influences and design
The name of Angela Orosco was derived from Angela Bennett, the name of the protagonist in the 1995 film The Net, and Laura's from the 1970 novel No Language But a Cry by Richard D'Ambrosio.
Music

At his home, Yamaoka took three days to write the music for "Theme of Laura", Silent Hill 2 ' s main theme, by combining "a sad melody" and "a strong beat", although he does not consider the melody to be the "most important" element of a musical piece.
Music
Silent Hill 2 makes extensive use of sound effects ranging from screams to footsteps on broken glass.
Music
Konami published Silent Hill 2 Original Soundtracks in Japan on October 3, 2001.
Music

Eight tracks ("Theme of Laura", "Null Moon", "Love Psalm", "True", "Promise", "Fermata in Mistic Air", "Laura Plays the Piano" and "Overdose Delusion") appeared in the 2006 PlayStation Portable release The Silent Hill Experience.
Music
In 2019, the soundtrack was re-released on vinyl by Mondo, who previously gave the same treatment to the soundtrack of Silent Hill in 2016.
Release
Silent Hill 2 was first released for the PlayStation 2 in North America on September 25, 2001, in Japan on September 27 and in Europe on November 23.
Release
An extended version of the game was published for Xbox in North America on December 18, 2001, Japan on February 22, 2002, and Europe on October 14.
Release
" Poem of the Last Moment ") in Japan, Restless Dreams in North America and Inner Fears in Europe.
Release
Creature Labs ported this edition to Windows, which Konami released in December 2002.
Release
Added features in the PC version include the ability to quicksave and watch trailers for Silent Hill 3.
Release
In 2018, Enhanced Edition mod was released for the PC version.
Release
In 2006, Konami re-released Silent Hill 2 with its indirect PS2 sequels, Silent Hill 3 and Silent Hill 4: The Room, in a bundle entitled The Silent Hill Collection in Europe and Japan.
Release
Silent Hill HD Collection, a compilation of remastered high-definition editions of Silent Hill 2 and 3, was released for the PlayStation 3 and the Xbox 360 on March 20, 2012.
Reception and legacy
Silent Hill 2 sold over one million copies in the month of its release in North America, Japan and Europe, with the most units sold in North America.
Reception and legacy
Rating aggregation site Metacritic shows "generally favorable reviews", with an average rating of 89 out of 100 for the PS2 version and 84 out of 100 for the Xbox version.
Reception and legacy
However, the PC port received "mixed or average reviews", with a Metascore of 70 out of 100.
Reception and legacy
Silent Hill 2 received praise from video game journalists at the time of its release and in retrospect.
Reception and legacy

The graphics and atmosphere of Silent Hill 2 were praised by reviewers, who highlighted the smooth transitions from computer-generated (CG) to in-game cutscenes and the sense of claustrophobia caused by the fog.
Reception and legacy

On the other hand, Thompson felt that the grainy image effects and dense fog hid the details of the environment, while Fielder wrote that the exterior environments "rarely push the PlayStation 2's graphical capabilities".
Reception and legacy
Reviewers have written that the PlayStation 2 and Xbox versions were mostly similar, except for the Born from a Wish side-scenario found in the Xbox version.
Reception and legacy
Conversely, Ron Dulin, another reviewer for GameSpot, wrote: "Not even the game's foggy atmosphere is thick enough to hide Silent Hill 2 ' s problems".
Reception and legacy
Silent Hill 2 is often considered to be one of the best horror games and one of the best video games of all time.
Reception and legacy
It ranked first on X-Play 's list of the scariest games of all time in 2006.
Reception and legacy
In 2009, IGN listed it as one of the five best horror video games created after 2000, and one of the twelve greatest PlayStation 2 games of all time.
Reception and legacy
It ranked again in IGN's list of the top 100 PS2 games, and again in 2018, on IGN ' s list of the 100 greatest video games ever made.
Reception and legacy
In a retrospective by GamePro, it was the 26th best game for the PS2.
Reception and legacy
In 2008, GamesRadar placed it on its list of the 15 best "video game stories" ever, describing it as "a punishing tale not easily matched".
Reception and legacy

In 2009, Wired News listed it as the 11th most influential game of the decade for its emphasis on psychological horror and exploration of taboo topics such as incest and domestic abuse, rather than gore.
Reception and legacy
In 2012, a top video games of all-time list by G4 television network ranked the game in 85th place.
Reception and legacy
That same year, the game's narrative was ranked first on GamesRadar's list of The Best Videogame Stories Ever.
Reception and legacy

Game Informer named Silent Hill 2 the best of the Silent Hill franchise and listed it as the second best horror game of all time in its October 2014 issue, and number eight on GameTrailers ' s Top Ten Twos list of the best second franchise games in 2015.
Remake
A remake was announced on October 19, 2022, during the Silent Hill Transmission event.
Remake
The remake will be developed by Bloober Team with contributions by original Silent Hill 2 artist Masahiro Ito and composer Akira Yamaoka.
Remake
It will be released for PlayStation 5 and Windows on October 8, 2024.
Film adaptation
In October 2022, it was announced that the game would be adapted into a film titled Return to Silent Hill, with Christophe Gans set to direct.

pst2_silent_hull_3.title: Silent Hill 3
sents: lead
Silent Hill 3 is a 2003 survival horror game developed by Team Silent, a group in Konami Computer Entertainment Tokyo, and published by Konami.
lead
The game was released from May to August, originally for the PlayStation 2.
lead

The third installment in the Silent Hill series and a direct sequel to the first Silent Hill game, it follows Heather, a teenager who becomes entangled in the machinations of the town's cult, which seeks to revive a malevolent deity.
lead

A port for Microsoft Windows was released later in November, and a remastered high-definition version was released as part of the Silent Hill HD Collection, for the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in 2012.
lead

Originally planned to be a rail shooter, as a result of the initially slow sales of Silent Hill 2 in Japan, Silent Hill 3 was developed almost simultaneously alongside another installment in the series, Silent Hill 4: The Room (2004).
lead
Among the influences on Silent Hill 3 are the film Jacob's Ladder and the works of horror novelist Stephen King.
lead
Its plot was loosely adapted into the 2012 film Silent Hill: Revelation.
Gameplay
Gameplay in Silent Hill 3 resembles closely that of its two predecessors, with gameplay set in the third-person view and divided among elements of combat, exploration, and puzzle-solving.
Plot
Silent Hill 3 takes place in the fictional universe of the Silent Hill series.
Plot
On the journey there, Heather learns from a journal left by Harry that she was the baby left to him at the end of the first Silent Hill game.
Plot
Because she is the reincarnation of Alessa, the girl originally intended to birth the cult's god, Claudia intends for her to bring forth the god.
Plot

Arriving in the seemingly abandoned and fog-shrouded town, Heather sets out to find a man named Leonard in a local hospital, being told by a member of the cult named Vincent that Leonard was in possession of a powerful magical sigil, the Seal of Metatron.
Plot
Revealed to be Claudia's abusive father, Leonard intends to dispose of Claudia as cult leader and attacks Heather after learning that she is not a member of the cult.
Plot
She journeys to the local church of the cult, through a local amusement park, at Douglas' request, according to Vincent, who despite being a member of the cult, opposes Claudia's goals.
Plot
Claudia is snatched away by an archangel of the cult to the chapel below, where she is found to have given birth and disappeared (with Heather presuming her dead).
Plot
The "Normal" ending, which is the only ending available on the first play-through of the game, sees Heather and Douglas survive, while in the "Possessed" ending, Heather kills Douglas.
Plot
In the "Revenge" ending, which is a joke ending accessible by performing certain in-game actions, Heather reunites with Harry, and Harry orders UFOs to blow up Silent Hill.
Development
Silent Hill 3 was created by Team Silent, a production group within Konami Computer Entertainment Tokyo.
Development
The development team for this iteration was smaller than that working on Silent Hill 2, with around 40 people working on the game, made up of the core team from the second title and some newcomers.
Development
Silent Hill 3 was originally planned to be a rail shooter, not a direct sequel to the first Silent Hill game, as a result of the initially slow sales and fan criticism of Silent Hill 2 in Japan.
Development

Eventually, the plan was discarded, with most of the early work produced between September 2001 and September 2002 being almost completely scrapped; although the concept of a Silent Hill rail shooter was later explored with Silent Hill: The Arcade in 2007.
Development
Silent Hill 3 ' s final version was developed from scratch in less than nine months, between September 2002 and May 2003.
Development

Like all Silent Hill games, one of Silent Hill 3 ' s influences is the film Jacob's Ladder: one of the subway platforms is named Bergen Street Station, the station Jacob was inquiring about at the beginning of the film.
Development
Silent Hill 3 incorporates references drawn from real-life actors and actresses.
Development
Claudia Wolf's character was considered the most difficult to design.
Development
She was first named "Christie", but it was deemed too "cute" and the character was eventually named after Italian actress Claudia Cardinale.
Development
A remastered high-definition version was released as part of the Silent Hill HD Collection, for the PlayStation 3 and the Xbox 360 on March 20, 2012.
Music
The soundtrack for Silent Hill 3 was composed by Akira Yamaoka.
Music
It was released in Europe on March 25, 2003 and in Japan on July 16, 2003.
Music
The song "You're Not Here" was included in the PS2 port of Dance Dance Revolution Extreme, and is also included in the Silent Hill Experience UMD media pack.
Music
The game's soundtrack is the first using vocals prominently.
Music

Most of the vocalized tracks are performed by Mary Elizabeth McGlynn (credited as Melissa Williamson); with Joe Romersa providing the chant on the track "Prayer" as well as the vocals on the ending theme " Hometown ".
Reception
Silent Hill 3 received positive reviews, garnering an 85/100 rating at Metacritic for the PlayStation 2 version, and a 72/100 rating for the PC version.
Reception

The story told as part of the atmosphere was also received positively, making for a "satisfying, coherent sequel", although its status as such meant that "it may be a little tough to follow for people who haven't played the first game", despite "a laudable effort to help people catch up".
Reception
Other criticism included the less compelling story compared to the first two entries.
Reception
Silent Hill 3 sold over 300,000 copies by November 2003.
Film adaptation
A film adaptation of Silent Hill 3, titled Silent Hill: Revelation 3D, was released on October 26, 2012, by Open Road Films.
Film adaptation
The film is a sequel to the film adaptation of the first installment in the Silent Hill series.

pst2_silent_hull_4.title: Silent Hill (video game)
sents: lead
Silent Hill is a 1999 survival horror game developed by Team Silent, a group within Konami Computer Entertainment Tokyo, and published by Konami.
lead
As the first installment in the Silent Hill video game series, the game was released exclusively for the PlayStation.
lead
Silent Hill uses a third-person view with real-time rendering of 3D environments.
lead
To mitigate the limitations of the console hardware, developers used fog and darkness to obscure the graphics and hide pop-ins, which, in turn, helped establish the game's atmosphere and mystery.
lead
Unlike earlier survival horror games that focused on protagonists with combat training, the player character of Silent Hill is an " everyman ".
lead
The game follows Harry Mason as he searches for his missing adopted daughter in the eponymous fictional American town of Silent Hill.
lead
Stumbling upon a cult conducting a ritual to revive a deity it worships, he discovers her true origin.
lead
Five game endings are possible, depending on the actions taken by the player, including one joke ending.
Gameplay
Accessible from the menu and readable only when sufficient light is present, each map is marked with places of interest.
Gameplay
The player finds a flashlight early in the game, which illuminates only a short distance.
Plot

Harry can later rescue Kaufmann from a monster, discover evidence of his involvement in local drug trafficking, and find his hidden bottle of aglaophotis, a supernatural liquid that can exorcise demons.
Plot
Alessa's never-healing wounds terrified her, and she fell deeper into a drug addiction fueled by Kaufmann.
Endings
The "Joke" ending features extraterrestrials abducting Harry.
Design
Despite the profit-oriented approach of the parent company, the developers of Silent Hill had considerable artistic freedom, as the game was produced in an era of lower-budget 2D titles.
Design
Toyama questioned Konami's decision to appoint him as director, as he had never directed a game before Silent Hill.
Design
The game's joke ending was inspired by a suggestion box created to find alternative explanations for the events in Silent Hill.
Design
As a young employee, Sato was initially limited to basic tasks such as font design and file sorting.
Design
He also created 3D demos and presentations and taught older staff members the fundamentals of 3D modeling.
Design
Sato eventually approached the company's higher-ups with a short demo movie he had rendered and threatened to withhold his technical knowledge unless he was assigned to 3D work.
Design
Over two and a half years, he lived in the development team's office, using approximately 150 Unix -based computers to render scenes after his coworkers left for the day.
Design
Sato estimated that the game's budget was lower than that of Japan's biggest games at the time.
Design
The game debuted at the 1998 Electronic Entertainment Expo in Atlanta, Georgia, where presentations of movies and in-game scenes received applause from the audience.
Design
Cheryl Mason's first name is based on actress Sheryl Lee, and Lisa Garland's surname is taken from actress Judy Garland.
Design
"Michael Kaufmann" combines the first name of Troma Studios producer Michael Herz and the surname of producer Lloyd Kaufmann.
Music
When he presented his compositions to the staff for the first time, they mistook the sound for a game bug.
Music
Yamaoka explained that the noise was intentional for the music, and the team only withdrew their objections after he elaborated on his reasons for this style.
Music
On March 5, 1999, the album Silent Hill Original Soundtracks was released in Japan.
Music
The 41st track, the ending theme "Esperándote," was composed by Rika Muranaka.
Music

When she arrived in Buenos Aires, Argentina, to record the translated Spanish lyrics with Argentine singer Vanesa Quiroz, Muranaka found that the syllables no longer matched the melody, and she had to recompose it in five minutes.
Music
On October 29, 2013, Perseverance Records released a "Best Of" album featuring 16 newly interpreted instrumental tracks composed by Akira Yamaoka and arranged and performed by Edgar Rothermich.
Music
The 17th track on the album is the ballad "I Want Love," performed by Romina Arena.
Release
Silent Hill was released for the PlayStation in 1999, with launch dates spanning from February to July in North America, Japan, and Europe.
Release
In 2006, it was included in the Silent Hill Complete Set in Japan.
Release
Silent Hill became available for download from the European PlayStation Network store for the PlayStation 3 and PlayStation Portable on March 19, 2009.
Release
On September 10, 2009, Silent Hill was released on the North American PlayStation Network. and it was re-released on the European PlayStation Network on October 26, 2011.
Adaptations
Titled Play Novel: Silent Hill, it was released only in Japan in 2001 as a gamebook -style visual novel.
Adaptations
A film adaptation, also titled Silent Hill, was released on April 21, 2006.
Adaptations
Directed by Christophe Gans, the film was loosely based on the game, incorporating elements from Silent Hill 2, Silent Hill 3, and Silent Hill 4: The Room.
Adaptations
The game was released on December 8, 2009, for the Wii and on January 19, 2010, for the PlayStation 2 and PlayStation Portable, to mostly positive reviews.
Reception and Legacy
The game sold over two million copies, which earned Silent Hill a spot in the American PlayStation Greatest Hits budget releases.
Reception and Legacy

In November 1999, the Verband der Unterhaltungssoftware Deutschland (VUD) awarded Silent Hill a "Gold" certification, indicating sales of at least 100,000 units across Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.
Reception and Legacy

House praised Silent Hill, describing it as "a truly magnificent work of art" and "a genuinely terrifying experience combined with a unique, gripping story and immersive atmosphere." However, the voice acting was less well-received.
Reception and Legacy
Reviewers noted that Silent Hill used real-time 3D environments, unlike the pre-rendered backgrounds found in Resident Evil.
Reception and Legacy
Despite this, most reviewers felt these factors enhanced the game's atmosphere.
Reception and Legacy
The game's lasting popularity as the first in the series was recognized long after its release.
Reception and Legacy

A 2000 list of the best PlayStation games by IGN ranked it as the 14th-best, while GameSpy 's 2005 article on the best PlayStation games placed Silent Hill as the 15th-best game produced for the console.
Reception and Legacy
In a 2006 GameTrailers video feature, Silent Hill was ranked number one on its list of the top ten scariest games of all time.
Reception and Legacy
In November 2012, Time named it one of the 100 greatest video games of all time.

pst2_disaster_reporter.title: Disaster Report
sents: lead

Disaster Report, known in Japan as Zettai Zetsumei Toshi (絶体絶命都市, The Desperate City) and in the PAL region as SOS: The Final Escape, is a PlayStation 2 survival action-adventure video game created by Irem.
lead
It was released in Japan in 2002 by Irem, and in North America and Europe in 2003, localized by Agetec.
lead

Guilty Gear is a series of fighting games by Arc System Works, created and designed by artist Daisuke Ishiwatari.
lead
The first game was published in 1998, and has spawned several sequels.
lead
It has also adapted to other media such as manga and drama CD.
lead
Guilty Gear has generally received praise from video game reviewers for its highly technical gameplay, graphics, soundtrack, and for its characters.
lead
Another fighting game franchise by Arc System Works, BlazBlue, is considered a spiritual successor of the series.
Synopsis

The story mostly focuses on Sol Badguy, a brash bounty hunter and die hard Queen enthusiast who, feeling guilty of his past creations which in turn, results in him becoming a gear, decides to make up for his own actions through fighting them whilst keeping his own identity a secret.
Synopsis
Throughout the story, Sol enacts his own vengeance upon That Man, who is mainly the cause behind most of the series conflicts, through killing him.
Synopsis

With it, Sol begins to realize that his own past is what deeply conflicts him the most, and through his past rivalries with Ky, as well as his relationships with the other characters, helps to overcome the enemy that he sorely sought to destroy in the first place.
Gameplay
Players are tasked with depleting their opponent's life gauge by utilizing attacks unique to each playable character.
Gameplay
In the case of timed matches, the player with the most remaining life when time runs out is the victor of that round.
Gameplay
The series' emphasis on speed and technicality and introduction of unique movement options such as an "air dash" would ultimately become the foundation for the "anime" subgenre of fighting games.
Gameplay

Guilty Gear X and later titles introduced more advanced techniques involving the Tension Gauge, such as the "Roman Cancel", allowing players to immediately stop the remaining animation of an attack, and "Dead Angle Attacks", counterattacks performed while a player is guarding.
Gameplay
Guilty Gear X2 introduced a "Burst Gauge" that slowly fills during the progression of a match.
Gameplay
Many characters also feature their own unique mechanics that differentiate them from each other.
Gameplay

For example, Zato-1 utilizes a shadow-like symbiotic creature named Eddie that is able to detach itself and be controlled separately for a period of time, allowing complex tandem attacks between the two.
Gameplay
Johnny carries a limited set of coins that can be thrown at the opponent.
Playable characters
Only playable in the PlayStation 2 version.
Playable characters
Only in the update version, Guilty Gear X Plus.
Playable characters
Only playable in the update/sequel version onward, Guilty Gear Xrd -REVELATOR-.
Playable characters
Only playable in the update/sequel version, Guilty Gear Xrd Rev 2.
Media

Two novelizations of Guilty Gear X were written by Norimitsu Kaihō, illustrated by Daisuke Ishiwatari, and published by Enterbrain: Lightning the Argent, and The Butterfly and Her Gale, on January 20, 2001 and on August 24, 2002.
Media
A manga titled Guilty Gear Xtra, a collaboration among Daisuke Ishiwatari, Norimitsu Kaihō, and Akihito Sumii, was serialized in Kodansha 's Magazine Z on September 22, 2003.
Media

2 —between October 24, and November 24, 2001, and two series of drama CDs based on Guilty Gear X2 were released by Team Entertainment: Red and Black —a series— were released in 2003 between July 16, and August 20.
Media
Another series of drama CDs, Night of Knives, was published in three volumes between October 20 and December 22, 2004.
Media

On February 11, 2017, Arc System Works announced a collaboration with Tecmo Koei 's Team Ninja to release Arc System Works Costume Set consisting the costumes of some characters from BlazBlue and Guilty Gear series in March 2017 for Dead or Alive 5: Last Round.
Media
Guilty Gear cosmetics are unlockable in the PC version of Them's Fightin' Herds for players that also own Guilty Gear Xrd Rev 2.
Media
An anime series, Guilty Gear Strive: Dual Rulers, was announced in June 2024, and is scheduled to premiere in 2025.
Reception and legacy
The Guilty Gear series is considered a cult classic among video game fans.
Reception and legacy

X ' s Dreamcast version has the highest score of the series as compiled by review aggregator GameRankings (89.33%), while X2 for PlayStation 2 occupies that position according to the other major aggregator, Metacritic (87).
Reception and legacy
On the other hand, the lowest score is given to Guilty Gear 2: Overture from both GameRankings (58.19%) and Metacritic (56/100).
Reception and legacy
Guilty Gear is considered by several sources to be the greatest 2D fighting game.
Reception and legacy

GameSpot said that " Guilty Gear is one of the few non- Capcom or SNK 2D fighters to make any sort of impact on the genre", while Eurogamer stated: "If 2D beat-em-ups are moving toward extinction, they really are ending on a high note with stuff like this." Its sequels were also well received.
Reception and legacy
GameSpy said " Guilty Gear X is hands-down the best 2D fighting game to date", and Guilty Gear X2 was described by About.com as "easily the best 2D fighter to come around in a long time."
Reception and legacy

Hampson included Guilty Gear among the 10 best fighting game franchises of all time, praising the series's evolution along the years, the "distinctive visual flair" of its 2D sprites, and the "well-defined story lines", adding "its identity is among the most unique in the world of beat-'em-ups."

Being a 3D game like Lament of Innocence before it, Curse of Darkness differs from its predecessor in a number of ways.

Curse of Darkness is set in the year 1479, three years after the events of Castlevania III: Dracula's Curse.
